units.la: Damit sie vermeint/ daß ein jedweder / der Tugendt unnd Redlig‐keit lieb hat/ der Danck‐barkeit sich zum höchsten befleissigen soll/ Sowol gegen denen/ die einem Gut: unnd Wolthat beweiset/ da sie schon nicht darumben ersucht worden. Als gegen dem jenigen/ den man darumb erbetten/ unnd es mit Mühe unnd Fleiß an jhn gelan‐gen lassen. Dann zu gleicher weise/ wie der unerbettene Wolthäter/ schier mehr Recht erlangt/ bey de‐nen/ so die Gutthat nicht gesucht/ als der jenige/ so darumben viel be‐grüsset unnd erbetten worden/ bey seinem Clienten oder Hülffgenossen/ rechts befinden vnd erlangen möge.
units.tr: So that they may consider that everyone who loves virtue and uprightness should devote himself most diligently to gratitude, both towards those who bestow a benefit or kindness even when they were not asked, and towards the one whom people have petitioned and whose favour has been won with effort and care. For just as the unasked benefactor almost gains more standing with those who did not seek his kindness than the one who has been courted and petitioned at length can secure from his client or helper.

units.la: Eben also vilmehr/ soll demselbigen/ Danck vnd Ehre bewisen werden/ so Wolthat vnd guten Willen/ vnersucht einem widerfahren lassen/ als dem andern/ der zuuor hero lange darumb ersucht worden.
units.tr: In the same way, and even more so, thanks and honour should be shown to the one who extends a kindness and goodwill unasked, than to the other who was long petitioned beforehand.

units.la: Aber zu einem Zweck kürtzlich zukommen/ Großgünstige Junckern/ vnd wolgeneigte Beförderer/ dieweil von EE: vnnd HHl. mir vor meine geringe Person/ auch meistentheils vnersucht/ vnderschidliche/ besonderbahre günstige Willen/ vnnd Beförderungen/ Allermeist aber/ in Liberey Sachen/ Bibliothecken schätzen/ Bücher kauffen/ rc. von ihnen widerfahren/ vnd mehrmaln erzeiget worden.
units.tr: But to come briefly to my purpose: most gracious gentlemen and well-disposed patrons, since from Your Excellencies and Honours there have been shown to me, in my humble person, and mostly unasked, various particular favourable intentions and promotions, above all in matters of the library, in valuing libraries, buying books, etc., and these have been shown and granted many times.

units.la: Als habe gegen dieselbigen Ihre Hl. Hl. ich es billicher / am billich / hinwider mit Danckbarkeit erkennen / vnd mit fast eben derglei‐chen dingen / vnnd Liberey-Händeln (weil ich vorhin Goldes vnnd Sil‐bers nit vil vberflüssig hab) vnd nach abermahligem Sprichwort. Als Wann S. Martin einem eine Ganß schencket/ So soll man jhn darzu zu gaste laden. Vnd Der Italiäner wurde schier sagen. Rendere Pan per Fugaccia.
units.tr: Since I cannot repay Your Most Serene Highnesses in kind, I acknowledge my debt to them with gratitude, and with almost the same sort of things and matters of the library (since I have little gold or silver to spare). Here again is the proverb: When St. Martin gives you a goose, you should invite him to dinner. And an Italian would almost say: Rendere Pan per Fugaccia.

units.la: Sie hiemit remuneriren, vnd dise Italiänische/meine geringfügen Bearbeiten/ jhnen / als derselbigen Sprachen vnd Sachen / wolgeüb‐ten / vnd mehr verständigen / auch dahero ohne zweifel/ hier zuvil belie‐bigen Personen / dediciren, zueig‐nen; vnd hiemit als fürnemme Pa‐tro
units.tr: I hereby repay them, and dedicate and consecrate to them this my humble work in Italian, as to persons well practised in those languages and subjects, more learned in them, and therefore without doubt very pleasing here. And so as distinguished patro-

units.tr: patrons, to defend them against my detractors. And I commend this small work of mine to their steadfast favour, humbly placing myself under their protection, and asking that they would be pleased to accept it.

units.la: Dem höchsten vnd Allmächtigen Herrn/ vor deroselben allerseits/ ferner Hülff vnd Segen / zu allem wol ergehn/ stättiglich bittende. Geben in Nürnberg den 1. Martij/ dises 1650. Jahrs. E. E. vnd Herrl. allezeit dienstgeflissner Joh. Guntzel. Civis Norib.
units.tr: I pray to the highest and almighty Lord for His continued help and blessing upon all of you, for all good success. Given at Nuremberg, 1 March, in the year 1650. Your Honours' ever devoted and obliged servant, Joh. Guntzel, citizen of Nuremberg.

units.la: DE LITERIS, von den Buchstaben.
units.tr: ON LETTERS, concerning the letters.

units.la: Litera, quibus vtuntur Itali, sunt viginti, A. B. C. D. E. F. G. H. I. L. M. N. O. P. Q. R. S, T. V. Z.
units.tr: The letters the Italians use are twenty: A. B. C. D. E. F. G. H. I. L. M. N. O. P. Q. R. S. T. V. Z.

units.la: Die Buchstaben, welche die Welschen gebrauchen, deren seynd zwaintzig, wie obstehet, Hae in quinq; vocales distinguuntur, nempe: A, E, I, O, V,
units.tr: The letters the Italians use are twenty in number, as stated above. Of these, five are distinguished as vowels, namely A, E, I, O, V.

units.la: Dife werden abgetheilet in fünffselbs lautende, als A, E, I, O, V, Et in confonantes: vt sunt re- liqua omnes, vnd in die mitlautende, als da seynd die andern allesambt.
units.tr: These are divided into the five self-sounding letters, A, E, I, O, V, and the consonants, which are all the rest; and the consonants are further divided into the half-sounding ones, which are all the others.

units.la: H. tamen non est Litera: sed aspirationis nota vel signum: Dochrift das H. kein Buchstab, sondern nur einer anhauchung, Kenn: oder Merkzeichen; oder verschnauffungs Merkzeichen, V, vero interdum consonans est: vt in istis dictionibus: Venere, Venus, Verita, Veritas, Virtu, Virtus, Vita, Vita.
units.tr: H is not a letter, but a mark of aspiration, a sign of breathing or a mark of pause. V, however, is sometimes a consonant, as in these words: Venere, Venus, Verita, Veritas, Virtu, Virtus, Vita, Vita.

units.la: Das V. aber ist bißweilen ein mitlautender Buchstab, als in difen Wörtern, Venere, Venus, &c. Id quod de Litera I, erit quoq; intelligendum, nam etsi in vocibus, quae a Latinis veniunt, incipientibus a Iu vel Ia, vel Io, vel IE, ei praeponatur Litera G, vt in istis vocibus videre est. Giouani, Iohannes. Giusto, Iustus, Giesu, Iesus, Giafone, Iafon. Welches auch von dem Buchstaben I. zuverstehen: Dann ob gleich in denen wörtern welche von den Lateinischen herkommen, vnd anfangs von einem IV, IA, oder IO, oder IE, der Buchstab G, vorgesetzt wurde, als in difen wörtern zusehen, Giouani, Iohannes, Giusto, Iustus, &c.
units.tr: V is sometimes a consonant letter, as in these words: Venere, Venus, etc. The same must be understood of the letter I. For although in words derived from Latin that begin with IU, IA, IO or IE, the letter G is placed before it, as can be seen in these words: Giouani (Iohannes), Giusto (Iustus), Giesu (Iesus), Giafone (Iafon), etc.

units.la: Nihil ominus, cum in pronunciando posteriori vocalis tantum audiatur sonus.
units.tr: Nevertheless, since in pronunciation only the sound of the latter vowel is heard,

units.la: Wirdt nichts desto weniger, weil im außspre- chen nur deß letzern selbstlautenden hall gehöret wirdt: Prior idcirco consonans ratione censebi-tur, der erste derohalben billich, vor einen mit-lautenden gehalten.
units.tr: the first is therefore rightly regarded as a consonant, so the first letter is justly counted among the consonants.

units.la: DE VSV LITERARVM.
units.tr: On the use of letters.

units.la: Von dem Gebrauch der Buchstaben.
units.tr: On the use of the letters.

units.la: Principio componunt Syllabas, ex quibus fiunt voces, sed id aly alter facinnt.
units.tr: First they combine syllables, from which words are formed, but some do this in different ways.

units.la: Erstlich setzen sie die Sylben zusamen, auß welchen die wörter entstehen. Aber dises thun etliche auff vnderschidliche weise, Nam vocales possunt omnes poni, tum in principio, tum in medio, tum in fine dictionis, quod apparet in ista voce, amore, amor.
units.tr: First they put syllables together, from which words arise, but some do this in different ways. For vowels can all be placed at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end of a word, as appears in this word, amore, amor.

units.la: Die selbst lautende, können so wol zu anfang, als in der mitten, vñ zu ende eines worts gesetzt werden, wie solches erscheinet an disem wort, amore, amor. At Consonantes ponuntur, vel in Principio, vel in medio, in fine autem per raro, vt infra ostendetur. Aber die mitlautende, werden entweder zu anfang oder in der mitten gesetzt, zu end aber gar selten, wie vnden soll gewisen werden.
units.tr: Vowels can be placed at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end of a word, as is shown in this word, amore, amor. But consonants are placed either at the beginning or in the middle, and only rarely at the end, as will be shown below. Consonants, however, are placed either at the beginning or in the middle, and only rarely at the end, as will be shown below.

units.la: Deinde nonnulla Consonantes ponuntur in Syllaba ante alias Conjonantes: aut B. ante R. in brene brevis, Tenebre, tenebra, libro, liber: & ante L. in oblio, oblinio, obliquo, obliquus, obligo, obligatio.
units.tr: Next, some consonants are placed in a syllable before other consonants: B before R, as in brene (breve, brief), Tenebre, tenebra, libro, liber; and before L, as in oblio, oblinio, obliquo, obliquus, obligo, obligatio.

units.la: Darnach werden etliche mitlautende in einer Sylben vor andere gesetzt, entweder ein B. vōt ein R. als in brève breuis, kurtz, Tenebre, Finsternuß, Libro, Buch, vnnd vor dem L. in oblio, vergeßlung, obliquo, vber zwerch, obligo, obligatio, verpflichtung.
units.tr: Next, some consonants are placed in a syllable before others: either B before R, as in brève, breuis, short; Tenebre, darkness; Libro, book; and before L in oblio, forgetfulness; obliquo, crosswise; obligo, obligatio, obligation.

units.la: Ferner wirdt gefunden, C. vor dem R. als in Crudele, greülich, credo, ich glaub, vnd vor dem L. in Clamore, geschrey. Inclito, Herrlich, oder fürtrefflich, Inclinato, auch Inchinato, geneigt, oder zugeneigt. Also auch in concludo, vnd conchiudo, ich beschließ, quamuis Conclusione & non Conchiusione recte dicatur, Ob man schon nicht Conchiusione sondern Conclusione fagt, so fagt man jedoch Italice conchiudo.
units.tr: Further, C is found before R, as in Crudele, cruel; credo, I believe; and before L in Clamore, outcry. Inclito, renowned or outstanding; Inclinato, also Inchinato, inclined or disposed. Likewise in concludo and conchiudo, I conclude. Although one correctly says Conclusione and not Conchiusione, yet, although one does not say Conchiusione but Conclusione, one nonetheless says Italice conchiudo in Italian.

units.la: D. ante R. in dritto, recht, rectus, Padre, Madre, Vatter, Mutter. Ladro, Dieb, vnnd dergleichen gefunden.
units.tr: D before R in dritto, right, rectus; Padre, father; Madre, mother; Vatter, Mutter (father, mother in German). Ladro, thief, and the like are found.

units.la: F. ante R. in Frutto, fructus, frucht, Fratello, frater, fraude, fraus.
units.tr: F before R in Frutto, fruit, fructus; Fratello, brother, frater; fraude, fraud, fraus.

units.la: Das F. wird vor dem R. gefunden, in frutto, Frucht, in fratello, Brüder, in fraude, betrug, &c.
units.tr: The F is found before R in frutto, fruit; fratello, brothers; fraude, deceit, etc.

units.la: G. ante N. in benigno, gütig, Ordigno, Werckzeug, oder Instrument, Ingegno, Ingenium, Gemüth oder verstand, Lamagna, Alemania, Teutschland, Compagno, Socius, Gesell. Et ante R. in Gratia, Gnad, Grato, angenemb, Grave, schwer, vnd vor dem L. ante L. in Gloria, Ruhm, preiß, Consiglio, Rathschlag, &c.
units.tr: G before N in benigno, kind; Ordigno, tool or instrument; Ingegno, Ingenium, mind or understanding; Lamagna, Alemania, Germany; Compagno, Socius, companion. And before R in Gratia, grace; Grato, agreeable; Grave, heavy; and before L in Gloria, glory or praise; Consiglio, counsel, etc.

units.la: P. ante R, in pregio, pretium, der wert, sempre allezeit, prudente, weiß: Lepre, Haas, Lepus, Et ante L, das P. vor dem L, in contemplo, ich betrachte wol, contemplor, item moltiplico, ich mache vil, ich manigfaltige, &c.
units.tr: P before R in pregio, pretium, worth; sempre, always; prudente, wise; Lepre, hare, Lepus. And before L, the P before L in contemplo, I contemplate well, contemplor; likewise moltiplico, I multiply, I make manifold, etc.

units.la: S. ante B. in Sbassamento, Dejecto, Niderwerfung, Sbandito, Exul, Außgetribener oder Verjagter, Et ante C. in Sacciato, außgejagt, eiectus, item nasco, nascor, ich wachse, pasco, ich weide. Et ante D. in indegno, Ira, Zorn, sdruccito, diffutus, auffgetrent, außgetrent, & ante F. in sfacendato, Ceffator, ein feyrender müßiger Mann, sfodrato, außgezogen, die Wöhr oder das Messer auß der Scheiden gezogen, districtus, vt ensis, Et S. ante G. in gomento, pauco ich erschrick, erzitter. Sganno, Latin. experior me a nemine fuisse deceptum, ich erfahre, daß ich von keinem bin betrogen worden, Et S. ante L. vor dem L. ist in sleale oder slegale, perfidus, trewloß, Slegato, folutus, auffgelöst, & ante M. Smembrato, zerzerrt, zerglidert, Lat. diffcerptus, Smorto, pallidus, Todtbleich, & ante N. in Sneruo, eneruo, ich schwäche, ich zerådere, Snello, Teütsch, schnell, (vna dictio) Lat. agilis, Snodo, enodo, ich löse den Knoten auff, & ante P. das S. ist in Spirito, Geist, Speranza, Hoffnung, Spes, S. ante Q. ist in Squalido, vnflätig, schmützig, Squame, Fischschupen, & ante R. in fregolato, diffolutus, vngezogen, entwicht, n.verderbt, Et ante T. das ist in studio, Fleiß, &c.
units.tr: S before B in Sbassamento, Dejecto, a casting down; Sbandito, Exul, one who is banished or driven out; and before C in Sacciato, driven out, eiectus; likewise nasco, nascor, I grow; pasco, I feed. And before D in indegno, Ira, anger; sdruccito, diffutus, torn open or ripped apart; and before F in sfacendato, Ceffator, an idle, lazy man; sfodrato, drawn out, the sword or knife pulled from its sheath, districtus, as a sword is. And S before G in gomento, pauco, I am startled, I tremble. Sganno, in Latin: I find that I have been deceived by no one. And S before L: before L in sleale or slegale, perfidus, faithless; Slegato, solutus, loosened. And before M, Smembrato, torn apart, dismembered, Latin diffcerptus; Smorto, pallidus, deathly pale. And before N in Sneruo, eneruo, I weaken, I unnerve; Snello, German schnell, quick (one word), Latin agilis; Snodo, enodo, I untie the knot. And before P, the S is in Spirito, spirit; Speranza, hope, Spes. S before Q is in Squalido, filthy, dirty; Squame, fish scales. And before R in fregolato, diffolutus, unrestrained, loose, dissolute. And before T, as in studio, zeal, etc.

units.la: T. ante R. in Tremo, ich zitter, Tronco, Block,
units.tr: T before R in Tremo, I tremble; Tronco, block,

units.la: Klotz, Tranquillitâ, Ruhe, ftilligkeit. Litera autem Z. neque precedit, neque sequitur aliam Consonantem, in eadem Syllaba. Aber der Buchstaben Z. gehet vor keinem her, so folget er auch auff keinen mitlautenden Buchstaben in einer Syllaben oder Buchstab begreiffung.
units.tr: log; Tranquillitâ, rest, stillness. But the letter Z neither precedes nor follows any other consonant in the same syllable. But the letter Z goes before no other letter, nor does it follow any consonant within one syllable or combination of letters.

units.la: Caterum, quod ad literas attinet, illud quoque mirum in modum nosse, operae pretium est. Ferners was die Buchstaben betrifft, ist dises auch sehr nothwendig zuwissen : Qua sane ratione duplicentur litera in dictione: was massen die mitlautende Buchstaben in einem Wort pflegen gedopelt zu werden. Id quod ordine literarum, quo facilius memoriae commendari possit, quam breviffime perseguar, welches ich nach ordnung der Buchstaben, damit es desto leichter müge begriffen werden, auff das allerkürtzeste durchgehen wil, B. itaque geminatur in iftis vocibus, wird derohalben das B. in difen Stimmwörtern gezwifachet, oder gedopelt, als Dubbio, dubium, zweiffel, debbo, debeo, ich soll, quod & deggio dicitur, so auch deggio gesagt wird. Sabbia, sabulum, Sandgries, Scabbia, scabies, Reüde, Krätze, item Abbete, Abies, Tannenbaum, Habbia, quod & haggia, habeat, daß er hab, Robba, Robbe, vestis vel fortuna, Haab vnnd Güetere, sed dicitur Rubare, furari, es wird aber gesagt stehlen, At labbro vel labrum, labum Bütte, Butte, Wasserkuffe, Fabro Schmidt, Libbro, Libro, ein Buch, Ebbro,
units.tr: Moreover, as regards letters, it is also very useful to know this well: by what reasoning consonants are doubled in a word, in what manner consonants are customarily doubled in a word. Which I shall go through as briefly as possible, in the order of the letters, so that it may be more easily grasped. B is therefore doubled in these words: Dubbio, dubium, doubt; debbo, debeo, I ought, which is also said deggio; so deggio is also said. Sabbia, sabulum, gravel sand; Scabbia, scabies, scab or itch; likewise Abbete, Abies, fir tree; Habbia, which is also haggia, habeat, that he may have; Robba, Robbe, vestis vel fortuna, goods and property; but it is said Rubare, to steal, furari. But labbro or labrum, labum, a vat, tub or water jug; Fabro, smith; Libbro, Libro, a book; Ebbro,

units.la: Ebbro, Ebrius, truncken, bezecht, possunt vel ita, vel simplici B. vt lubebit, scribi, können entweder also, oder nur mit einem einfachen B. geschriben werden.
units.tr: Ebbro, Ebrius, drunk, intoxicated. They may be written either thus or with a single B, as one pleases. They may be written either this way or with a single B, as one likes.

units.la: Geminatur item in tertijs Persons, praeteriti imperfecti, subiunctiui modi, tam singularis quam pluralis num. vt Item in der dritten Person des praeteriti imperfecti coniunctiui, so wol in singulari als in plur. num. werden auch gedopelt : Als Amerebbe & Amerebbono, daß er liebete, daß sie liebete, Lat. amaret & amarent, Item valerebbe, valerebbono, daß er sich wol gehabe, idem daß er gelte, daß sie vil vermögen oder gelten, Lat. valeret, valerent. Idem, Leggerebbe, & Leggerebbino, Vdirebbe, & vdirebbono, hoc est, Legeret, & legerent. Audiret & audirent, das ist, da der laße, da difelafen, da er höret, da sie höreten.
units.tr: B is likewise doubled in the third persons of the imperfect subjunctive, both singular and plural, as Also doubled in the third person of the imperfect subjunctive, in both the singular and the plural, as: Amerebbe and Amerebbono, that he would love, that they would love, Lat. amaret and amarent; likewise valerebbe, valerebbono, that he might fare well, or that he might be worth something, that they might be of great worth or value, Lat. valeret, valerent. Likewise Leggerebbe and Leggerebbino, Vdirebbe and vdirebbono, that is, legeret and legerent. Audiret and audirent, that is, that he would read, that they would read, that he would hear, that they would hear.

units.la: Rursus geminatur, in ista voce, widerumb wird der Buchstaben B. gedopelt, in dem wort Obietto, qua & oggietto dicitur, hoc est obiectum, ein ding, materi, damit man vmbgehet.
units.tr: Again it is doubled in this word: the letter B is doubled in the word Obietto, which is also called oggietto, that is, obiectum, a thing or matter with which one deals.

units.la: Item in nonnullis verbis, qua componuntur ex ad, praepositione, mutata litera D. in B. ex qua incipiunt simplicia, vt &c. So wol in etlichen wörtern, so mit der Praepositiõn ad zusamen gesetzt seynd, da der Buchstab D. in ein B. von welchem die einfachen verba anfangen, verwandelt wird.
units.tr: Likewise in some words compounded of ad, the preposition, where the letter D is changed into B, the letter with which the simple verbs begin, as etc. So also in some words compounded with the preposition ad, where the letter D is changed into B, the letter with which the simple verbs begin.

units.la: Als Barbaglio, hoc est Lat. offusco, ich dunckel-
units.tr: Barbaglio, that is, in Latin offusco, I darken-

units.la: färbe oder schwärtze, Abbraccio, ampleßor, ich vmbfahe: Excluduntur, es werden hiebey ausgeschlossen, Abondo, Lat. abundo, ich gehe vber, ich fliesse vber, Abandono. derelinquo, ich hinderlasse, C. autem geminatur, in ijs dictionibus, quae deducuntur a latinis habentibus literam X. in prima Syllaba, atq; ex excellens sit eccellente, ex excepto, Eccetto, & Exceptio, Eccentione. NB.
units.tr: or blacken; Abbraccio, amplector, I embrace. These are excluded here. Abondo, Latin abundo, I overflow; Abandono, derelinquo, I abandon. C is doubled in those words which derive from Latin words having X in the first syllable, and so excellens becomes eccellente, excepto becomes eccetto, and exceptio becomes eccentione. N.B.

units.la: Das C. aber wird gedopelt in denen wörtern, so von den Lateinischen herkommen, vnd in der ersten Sylben den Buchstaben X. haben, vnd wird alfo von dem wort excellens, Excellente, fürtrefflich, & excepto, eccetto, & exceptio, eccentione, Außnemmung, oder vorbehaltung.
units.tr: The C, however, is doubled in words that come from Latin and have X in the first syllable. Thus from excellens comes Eccellente, excellent or magnificent; and from excepto comes eccetto, and exceptio, eccentione, exception or reservation.

units.la: Inque iftis vocibus, vnnd in diefen wörtern, Occhio, Oculus, Auge, Ginocchio, genu, Knye, qua habent in plurali, occhi, oculi, Augen, Ginocchi, genua, die Knye, ita finocchio, faniculus, & finocchi, faniculi, Alfo auch der vnd die Fenchel, Verum illud hic obiter annotabo, Dises aber muß ich allhie ein wenig erinnern, Syllabam chi, dulcius in his dictionibus esse pronunciandam: daß die Sylbe chi, in difen wörtern müsse etwas lieblicher außgesprochen werden, quam in flocchi, enfes, Fiocchi, flocci, Als in den Schwertern, gezuckten wöhren, Schneeflocken, Wollflocken, quo in fingulari ... lari alioqui habent, flocco, enfis, welche sonsten in fingulari haben, gezuckt Schwert, Schneeflock, Wolleflock. Sed hanc rationem pronunciandi, scripto quis docere, non potest, Aber dise art außzuredẽ,kan keiner schrifftlich lehren.
units.tr: And in these words, Occhio, Oculus, eye; Ginocchio, genu, knee; which have in the plural occhi, oculi, eyes; Ginocchi, genua, knees; so finocchio, faniculus, and finocchi, faniculi, fennel, both masculine and feminine. But this I will note here in passing: that the syllable chi must be pronounced somewhat more softly in these words, than in flocchi, enfes, Fiocchi, flocci, which mean swords, drawn blades, snowflakes, tufts of wool, which in the singular otherwise have flocco, enfis, a drawn sword, a snowflake, a tuft of wool. But no one can teach this manner of pronunciation in writing.

units.la: Geminatur insuper hæc litera in distionibus, Vber disz werden auch gedopelt in disen wörtern, als, Sacco, ein Sack, (ist gleich in vilen Sprachen,) item giaccio, jaceo, ich lige, ghiaccio, glacies, Eyß, Pariter in verbis compositis, ex præpositione ad, mutata D. in C. velut nuper diximus de Litera B. Gleicher weise in denen zusamen gesezten wörtern, auß der præpositione ad, da das D. ist in ein C. verwandlet worden, wie wir oben gesagt von dem Buchstaben B. Als, Accoglio, excipio, ich empfah oder nimm auff; Accenno, ich falle bey mit wincken, innuo; Accopio, copulo, ich baare zusamen, ich kuppele zusam, Demum in verbis incipientibus à Ra, vt Rac. &c. So dann auch in denen wörtern, so sich anfahen von dem Ra, als, Racconciare, reficere, wider ersetzen, außbessern, item Raccommandare, commendare, rühmen, lobsprechen.
units.tr: This letter is further doubled in words such as Sacco, a sack (this is the same in many languages); likewise giaccio, jaceo, I lie down; ghiaccio, glacies, ice. Likewise in compound words formed with the preposition ad, where D is changed into C, as we said recently of the letter B: Accoglio, excipio, I receive or take in; Accenno, innuo, I signal by a nod; Accopio, copulo, I couple or join together. Finally in words beginning with Ra, such as Racconciare, to mend or repair again; likewise Raccommandare, to commend, to praise.

units.la: D. proinde est duplex, in cadde, quod est præteritum perfectum, indicatiui modo, ac tertia persona, singul. num. verbi cado, vel caggio, hoc est cado, & in caddero, plur. num, hoc est ceciderunt, Ist demnach das D. gedopelt in dem wort cado oder caggio, daß ist ich falle, & in caddero plur. num. daß ist ceciderunt, sie seynd gefallen.
units.tr: So D is doubled in cadde, which is the perfect past, indicative mood, third person singular of the verb cado or caggio, that is, I fall; and in caddero, plural, that is, ceciderunt, they have fallen.

units.la: Geminatur item in verbis compositis, ex præpositione. fitione ad, vt sunt, Adduco, Addormo, Addol-cisco.
units.tr: D is also doubled in compound verbs formed with the preposition ad, as are Adduco, Addormo, Addolcisco.

units.la: Das D. wird gleichfalls gedopelt, in den zu-sam gesezten wörtern, Adduco, ich führ herbey, Addormo, ich wird schläfferig, Addolcisco, ich verstiesse, mach sieß, Ita & in verbo Raddolcire, vnd also auch in dem wort Raddolcire, verstiessen, item versönen, vergleichen.
units.tr: D is likewise doubled in compound words formed with ad: Adduco, I lead to; Addormo, I grow drowsy; Addolcisco, I sweeten, I make sweet. So also in the word Raddolcire, to sweeten, and also to appease or reconcile.

units.la: Porro F. ponitur duplex in istis vocibus, Vber dieß wird ein zweyfach F. gesezt in disen wörtern, Offesa, Beleidigung, Vfficio, Ambt, Besse, Spottreden, Affanno, Bekümmernuß, & huius modi quam plurimis, vnd dergleichen mit gar vil andern mehr,
units.tr: Moreover, F is doubled in these words: Offesa, offence; Officio, office; Besse, mockery; Affanno, anxiety, and very many others of this kind.

units.la: Item in verbis compositis ex prapositione ad, vt affermo, Affretto, Accelero, Deßgleichen in zu-sam gesezten wörtern, auß der prapositione ad, ist Affermo, ich bejahe, bestettige, in Affretto, ich eyle. Idem intelligatur de verbis compositis ex prapositione Di, vt differisco, Diffido, Diffinisco, Difes ist auch zuverstehen, von denen wörtern, so auß der prapositione Di, zusamen gesetzt werden, als Differisco, ich schieb auff, Diffido, ich mißtraw, Diffinisco, ich beschreib oder beschieß eigentlich, Ita & de nonnullis verbis ducentibus originem a latinis verbis, qua habent prima Syllaba prapofit, Ob, mutata B. in F. hoc modo, offero, offendo, offusco, Wie auch nicht weniger von etlichen wörtern, so jhren vrsprung von den Lateinischen
units.tr: Likewise in compound verbs formed with the preposition ad: affermo, I affirm, confirm; Affretto, I hasten; Accelero, I accelerate. The same is to be understood of compound verbs formed with the preposition Di, such as Differisco, I postpone; Diffido, I distrust; Diffinisco, I define or, more exactly, I describe. So also with some words derived from Latin whose first syllable has the prefix Ob, where B is changed into F in this way: offero, offendo, offusco. Likewise, not less, in some words that take their origin from Latin,

units.la: haben, wird in der erften Sylben der præpofition das B. in ein F. verwechßelt, auff dife weife, Offero, offendo, &c. ich erbiete, ich beleidige, ich verdunckle, Præterea G. duppli c arı folet, quoties I. & O. vel I. & A. in diphthongum coalescunt, ita vt vnam efficiant syllabam: Vber das pflegte das G. gedoppelt zuwerden, so offt das I. vnnd O. oder das I. vnnd A. in einen zweylautenden, halb Buchstaben, gleichsam zusamen wachsen, also daß sie eine Silben machen, Quemadmodum vi-dere est, in istis vocibus, Wie dann zusehen ist, in disen wörtern, Saggio, saggia, sapiens, weise, quæ habent in plur. saggi & sagge, die weisen.
units.tr: in the first syllable of which the prefix is changed from B to F, in this way: Offero, offendo, &c.: I offer, I offend, I obscure. Moreover, G is customarily doubled whenever I and O, or I and A, coalesce into a diphthong, so that they make one syllable. As may be seen in these words, Saggio, saggia, sapiens, wise, which in the plural have saggi and sagge, the wise.

units.la: Hic notandum perperam a nonnullis collocatum, inter G. & B. huius postremæ vocis, nempe sagge, & similium, literam I. vt dicant.
units.tr: Here it must be noted that some have wrongly placed the letter I between G and E in this last word, namely sagge, and similar words, so that they say

units.la: Allhier ist zumercken, daß von etlichen zwi- schen dem G. vnd E. difes letzten worts, nem- lich sagge, ein I. vergeblich hinein gesetzt wird, daß sie sagen, Saggie, Piaggie, Greggie, cum dicen- dum sit, da sie sagen sollen sagge, sapientes, die weisen, Piagge, Ora, Littora, die Grentzen, Ge- statten, Wasserufer &c. Gregge, Grex, die Herde, At contra, quando I. & O. duas efficiunt syllabas, G. præcedere erit simplex, Hingegen aber wenn das I. vnd O. zwo Sylben machen, so gehet ein- fach G. vorher, als Priuilegio, Freyheit, Regio, Königisch, Litigio, ich hadere, vestigio, fuß- stapffe, &c.
units.tr: Here it should be noted that some foolishly insert an I between the G and E of this last word, namely sagge, saying Saggie, Piaggie, Greggie, when they should say sagge, sapientes, the wise; Piagge, ora, littora, the borders, shores, river banks, etc.; Gregge, grex, the flock. On the other hand, when I and O make two syllables, a single G comes before them, as in Priuilegio, freedom; Regio, royal; Litigio, I quarrel; vestigio, footstep, etc.

units.la: Alfo fagen wir auch, Dionigio, & Dionigi, Ambrogio, Dionifius & Ambrofius. Neque ferit bitur duplex G. in illis vocibus, qua duplicitur in I, terminantur.
units.tr: So too we say Dionigio and Dionigi, Ambrogio, Dionysius and Ambrosius. G is not doubled in those words that end in a double I.

units.la: Es wird auch kein zwifaches G. gefchriben, in denen wörtern, welche auff zwey I. fich enden, vt funt Parifi, & Parigi, Parifij, Tunifi, & Tunigi, Luifi, & Luigi, Maiagifi, & Malagigi, als da feynd Paris, Tunis, Ludwig vnd Malage‑fer, &c. Verum reperitur duplex in illis, qua ex Latinis veniunt, definentibus in literam X. Aber ein zwifaches G. wird in denen gefunden, welche von den Lateinifchen, fo auff ein X. außgehen, als Grex, Gregge, greggia, ein Herde; item Legge, Lex, Gefätz, &c. Sed ex, Fex fit feccia, Heffen, quod latinum in genitiuo fingulari habeat fecis, weil das Lateinifche im Genitiuo fingulari hat fecis, der Heffen.
units.tr: Nor is a double G written in words that end in two I's, such as Parisi and Parigi, Parisij, Tunisi and Tunigi, Luisi and Luigi, Malagigi and Malagigi, which are Paris, Tunis, Lewis, Malaga, etc. But a double G is found in words that come from Latin and end in X, such as Grex, Gregge, greggia, a flock; likewise Legge, Lex, law, etc. But from Fex comes feccia, dregs, because the Latin has fecis in the genitive singular, of the dregs.

units.la: Ex Rex autem fit Rè, tam pro fingulari, quam pro plurali, von dem wörtlein Rex aber wird Rè, einKönig, fo wol in infingul. als purali num, wie wol die Poeten zuweilen fagen, in plurali Regi, & fi Poeta in plur. dicant quandoque Regi, &c.
units.tr: From Rex, however, comes Rè, a king, both in the singular and in the plural, although the poets sometimes say Regi in the plural, and the poet sometimes says Regi in the plural, etc.

units.la: Duplicantur etiam in quibufdam verbis definen‑tibus in Go, Es wird auch gedoppelt in etlichen wörtern, fo auff ein Go außgehen: als Leggio, ich lefe, correggo, ich verbeffere, veggo, quod & veggio, ich fehe.
units.tr: G is also doubled in certain verbs ending in -Go, such as Leggio, I read; correggo, I correct; veggo, also written veggio, I see.

units.la: Tandem conduplicantur, in verbis compofitis, ex prapo
units.tr: Finally, they are doubled in compound verbs formed from the prepo-

units.la: præpositione ad, cuius modi sunt, Letztlich wird das G. zwyfach gesetzt, in denen wörtern, so mit der præpositione ad, zusam gefüget werden, als da seynd, Agghiaccio, ich gefrüre zusam, oder ich gefrüer, Aggiungo, ich füege hinzu, Aggua-glio, ich vergleiche, & Aggiornarsi, tagen, Tag werden,
units.tr: With the preposition ad, of which kind are these: finally G is doubled in words compounded with the preposition ad, such as Agghiaccio, I freeze together, or I am frozen; Aggiungo, I add; Agguaglio, I compare; and Aggiornarsi, to dawn, to become day.

units.la: Sequitur L. quod duplex reperitur in istis dictio-nibus, Folget das L. welches zweyfach gefun-den wird in disen wörtern, als Bello, Castello, Fra-tello, Fallo, Canallo, metallo, &c. Schön, Schloß, Bruder, Fehler, Roß, Ertzzeug, &c. & huiusmodi fexcentis, vnd dergleichen vnzehlich mehr.
units.tr: It follows L., which is found doubled in these words: Bello, Castello, Fratello, Fallo, Canallo, metallo, etc. (beautiful, castle, brother, fault, horse, tool, etc.), and huiusmodi sexcentis, and countless more like them.

units.la: Reperitur deinceps geminata in tertijs persoais fingul. num. præteriti indicatiui, eor. verbor. quæ prima & quarta sunt conjugationis, quando in fine adjunguntur articuli, Darnach wirds auch ge-doppelt gefunden, in denen tertijs persoais fingul. num. præteriti indicat. derer wörter, nemblich, welche in die erste vnd vierte Conjugation gehö-ren, wenn zu end die articul angefuegt werden, als Amollo, Vdllo, hab jhn geliebt, hab jhn ge-hört, Geminatur etiam in verbis compositis, ex præ-positione ad, Das L. wird auch zweyfach ge-macht, welche in denen verbis, mit der præposi-tione ad, zusamen gesetzt werden, als Allargo, Alleuio, Alloggio, Alletto, Allento, &c. Ich erwei-tere, erleuchtere, mache breit, ich herbrige, ich ätze an, ich laß nach, &c, Id ipsum sit tandem. in ver in verbis, quibus praeponitur Ra, Eben dies ge-fchicht in denen verbis, denen das Ra wird vor-gesetzt, als da ist, vt est, Rallento, Rallegro, Rallu-mo, ich lasse nach, mach fröliche, erleucht wider, Caeterum minime pratermiserim in profa scribi folere, a plerisque, Letzlichen kan ich keines weegs mit still-schweigen vbergehen, in der gemeinen Text-schrifft, oder so nicht verß weiß ist, die meisten pflegen zuschreiben, als da ist, Dello, Allo, Dallo, Delli, Alli, Dalli, Della, Alla, Dalla, delle, Alle, & dalle, pro Delo, Alo, Dalo, Deli &c. quomodo scribunt Poeta, wie die Poeten schreiben, sed Allui, Dallui & huiusmodi non vteret, etsi nonnulli probent, Aber Allui, Dallui, vnd dergleichen wolt ich nit gern gebrauchen, ob gleich etliche solches billich-ten.
units.tr: It is further doubled in the third person singular of the preterite indicative of those verbs that belong to the first and fourth conjugations, when the articles are added at the end: as Amollo, Vdllo (I have loved him, I have heard him). It is also doubled in verbs compounded with the preposition ad: as Allargo, Alleuio, Alloggio, Alletto, Allento, etc. (I widen, I lighten, I make broad; I lodge, I entice, I slacken, etc.). The same occurs in verbs to which Ra is prefixed, vt est: Rallento, Rallegro, Rallumo (I slacken, I make merry, I light up again). Finally, I cannot pass over in silence that in prose, that is, in ordinary writing not in verse, most people write Dello, Allo, Dallo, Delli, Alli, Dalli, Della, Alla, Dalla, delle, Alle, and dalle, for Delo, Alo, Dalo, Deli, etc., as the poets write, but Allui, Dallui and the like I would not willingly use, though some approve of them.

units.la: Quantum vero attinet ad literam M. ea gemina-tur in istis, Was aber den Buchstaben M. ange-het, wird derselbig gedoppelt in disen wörtern, Damma, Epigramma, Fiamma, Giemma, Gierusa-lemme Boemme, Item duplicantur, cum particula Mi, apponitur verbo in fine, Item das M. wird gedoppelt, wenn das kleine Stuckwörtlein mi, dem verbo zu ende wird angehengt, als Emmi, hoc est, est mihi, ist mir, Dammi, damihi, gib mir, fammi, facmihi, thue mir, &c.
units.tr: As for the letter M, it is doubled in these words: Damma, Epigramma, Fiamma, Giemma, Gierusalemme, Boemme. It is also doubled when the little particle mi is appended to the end of a verb: as Emmi, hoc est, est mihi (it is to me); Dammi, da mihi (give me); fammi, fac mihi (do for me), etc.

units.la: Item in primis personis num. multitud. praeteri-torum modi indicat, Mehr in primis personis plur. num. num. in dem anzeig modo, ist das M. doppelt, als Amámmo, Amauimus, wir haben geliebt, Valem-mo, valuimus, wir feynd wol auff gewefen, Le-gemmo, Legimus, wir haben gelesen, Vdimmo, audiuimus, wir haben gehört, fummo, fuimus, wir feyn gewefen.
units.tr: Also, in the first persons plural of the indicative mood of the preterites, the M is doubled: as Amámmo, Amauimus (we have loved); Valemmo, valuimus (we have been well); Legemmo, Legimus (we have read); Vdimmo, audiuimus (we have heard); fummo, fuimus (we have been).

units.la: Item in verbis compositis ex praepositione ad, vt, &c. Mehr in den wörtern, so mit der praepositio-ne ad, zusamen gesetzt feyn, als Ammaestro, eru-dio, ich vnderweise, vnderrichte, oder lehre, Ammonisco, moneo, ich vermahne, Ammiro, admiror, ich verwundere, Rammentare, memorare, gedencken, Immergere, eintauchen, Caterum N. est duplex in istis nominibus, Ferner ist das N. zwyfach in difen Namen, als Donna, Madonna, eine Fraw, Sonna, Anno, Iahr, Affanno, Bekümmernuß, Inganno, Betrug, Senno, Sinn, Innocente, vnschuldig.
units.tr: Also in verbs compounded with the preposition ad, vt, etc.: as Ammaestro, erudio (I instruct, I train, or I teach); Ammonisco, moneo (I admonish); Ammiro, admiror (I marvel); Rammentare, memorare (to remember); Immergere (to immerse). Moreover, N is doubled in these names: as Donna, Madonna (a lady); Sonna, Anno (year); Affanno (distress); Inganno (deceit); Senno (sense); Innocente (innocent).

units.la: Duplicatur quoque in ijs dictionibus, quae derivantur a latinis nominibus, in quibus M. praecedit, N. vt &c. Es wird das M. auch gedoppelt, in denen Namen, welche von den Lateinischen herkommen, in welchem das M. vor dem N. hergehet, als Sonno, somnus, Schlaff, Colonna, Columna, Seul, Danno, Damnum, Schad, Scanno, Scamnum, Banck, Autunno, Autumnus, Herbst, vnd vil andere dergleichen.
units.tr: It is also doubled in those words derived from Latin nouns in which M precedes N, vt, etc. The M is also doubled in names that come from the Latin, where M comes before N, as Sonno, somnus (sleep); Colonna, columna (pillar); Danno, damnum (harm); Scanno, scamnum (bench); Autunno, autumnus (autumn); and many others like these.

units.la: Item evenit in tertijs personis, plur. num. praesent, indicat. verborum, quae in prima persona sin-gul. in gul. monosyllaba sunt, Difes geschicht auch in denen tertiis personis, plur. num. indicat. modi, in den Wörtern, welche in der ersten Person des sin-gul. num. nur eine Sylben haben, alsdann seyn, in Ho, habeo, ich hab, hat in plur. hanno, habent, sie haben, vnd Sto, ich stehe, in plural. lat. stant, stanno, sie stehen, vnd fo, facio, ich thue, fanno, sie thun, faciunt lat. & do, ich geb, danno, sie geben, dant, lat. excipitur, es wird hie ausgenommen, So, sum, ich bin, daffelbige hat in plur. sono, mit einem N, (sunt lat.) sie seyn.
units.tr: This also happens in the third persons plural of the present indicative of verbs that are monosyllabic in the first person singular: thus in Ho, habeo (I have), and in the plural hanno, habent (they have); and Sto (I stand), in the plural stant, stanno (they stand); and fo, facio (I do), fanno (they do), faciunt in Latin; and do (I give), danno (they give), dant in Latin. An exception is made here: So, sum (I am), which in the plural has sono, with one N (sunt in Latin; they are).

units.la: Habent quoque geminum N, tertia item persona plur. num. futuri indicat. Als ameranno, amabunt, sie werden lieben, valeranno, valebunt, sie werden gelten, oder wolstehen, Leggeranno, sie werden lesen, Vdiranno, sie werden hören.
units.tr: They also have a double N in the third person plural of the future indicative: as ameranno, amabunt (they will love); valeranno, valebunt (they will be worth, or be well); Leggeranno (they will read); Vdiranno (they will hear).

units.la: Scribuntur pariter per duplex N, hæc præterita in sing. num. Gleicher weise werden mit zweyen N, geschriben, dise perfecta sing. num. Als venni, veni, ich bin kommen, venne, venit, er ist kommen, item tenne, tenui, ich hab gehalten, tenne, tenuit, er hat gehalten, vnd in plur. vennero, venerunt, sie seynd kommen, tennero, tenuerunt, sie haben gehalten.
units.tr: These perfects in the singular are likewise written with a double N: as venni, veni (I have come); venne, venit (he has come); also tenne, tenui (I have held); tenne, tenuit (he has held); and in the plural vennero, venerunt (they have come); tennero, tenuerunt (they have held).

units.la: Item in verbis compositis, ex præpositione ad, vt, wie auch in denen wörtern, so mit der præpositione ad, seynd zusamen gesetzt, als Annoctarfi, noctescere, nachten, Nacht werden, Annidarfi, in nido se collocare, sich in das Nest setzen,
units.tr: Also in verbs compounded with the preposition ad, vt: as Annoctarsi, noctescere (to grow night, to become night); Annidarsi, in nido se collocare (to settle in the nest);

units.la: Annuncio, Nuntio, ich verkünde, Annullare, vernichten.
units.tr: Annuncio, nuntio (I announce); Annullare (to annul).

units.la: Demum gĕmĭnātur, in verbis compositis, ex præpositione In, vt innouare & innamorarsi, & multa alia, &c.
units.tr: Finally, it is doubled in verbs compounded with the preposition In, vt innouare and innamorarsi, and many other words, etc.

units.la: Endtlich wird es gedoppelt in denen verbis, so mitelst præpositione In, zusam gefügt werden, als innouare, verneuwern, & innamorarsi, sich verlieben, vnd vil andere mehr. Iam sequitur P. quod duplex recipitur, à vocibus Zoppo, claudu. Ietzund folget das P. welches zweyfach genommen wird, in den Wörtern, Zoppo, hinckend, Lahm, Appetito, Begierd, Doppio, duplex, gedoppelt, doppelt, Coppia, ein baar, als ein baar gute Männer, vt duo probi viri, vna Coppia d' huomini da bene, item doppo, post, nach, etliche schreiben auch dopo, als die Poeten vnd andere.
units.tr: Finally, it is doubled in verbs compounded with the preposition In, as innouare (to renew) and innamorarsi (to fall in love), and many others. Now follows P, which is taken doubled from the words Zoppo, claudus (lame, limping); Appetito (appetite, desire); Doppio, duplex (double); Coppia (a pair, as a pair of good men, vt duo probi viri, vna Coppia d' huomini da bene); also doppo, post (after). Some also write dopo, as do the poets and others.

units.la: Geminatur etiam in istis prateritis. Es wird auch in disen prateritis gedoppelt, als ruppi, rupi, ich hab gerissen, oder zerrissen, ruppe, rupit, er hat gerissen, rupperò, ruperunt, sie haben gerissen, ita seppi, sciui, seppe, sciuit, ich hab, er hat gewust, seppero, sciuerunt, sie haben gewust, ita sappia, sciam, also auch, daß ich wisse, egli sappia, sciat, daß er wisse, sappiamo, sciamus, daß wir wissen, oder wir sollen wissen, & sappiate, sciatis, ihr sollet wissen, sappiano, scient, sie sollen wissen. Item fit in quibusdam hominibus proprijs, vt Filippo, Aristippo, &c. dassel-
units.tr: It is also doubled in these preterites: as ruppi, rupi (I have broken or torn); ruppe, rupit (he has broken); rupperò, ruperunt (they have broken); so seppi, sciui (I have known), seppe, sciuit (he has known); seppero, sciuerunt (they have known); so sappia, sciam (that I may know); egli sappia, sciat (that he may know); sappiamo, sciamus (that we may know, or we should know); sappiate, sciatis (you should know); sappiano, scient (they should know). The same happens in certain proper names of men, vt Filippo, Aristippo, etc., the same-

units.la: bige geschicht auch in etlichen eigenen Man-nes Namen, als Egisippo, Ippolito, Ippodamia, Gioseppe, vnd dergleichen.
units.tr: thing also happens in certain men's proper names, as Egisippo, Ippolito, Ippodamia, Gioseppe, and the like.

units.la: Item in verbis compositis, ex praposit. ad, vt, mehr in denen Wörtern, so mit der prapositione ad sein zusamen gefetzt, als approuo, probo, ich halt vor gut, appare, daß ersich erzeig, che egli s' appare, daß er erschein.
units.tr: Also in verbs compounded with the preposition ad, vt: as approuo, probo (I approve); appare (that he appears, shows himself); che egli s'appare (that he appear).

units.la: Et in ijs, qua ex Ra componuntur, vnd in de-nen, welche mit dem Ra seynd zusamen gefetzt, vt rapporto, ich bring, refero, rapello, ich wider-ruffe, renoco, Et tandem in verbo oppongo, oppono, vnd endtlich in dem Wort, C.p.pongo, ich setz entgegen. Neq; prateribo literam Q. velut qua & si non geminatur in aliqua distione, si scripturam spestemus. Ich will auch den Buchstaben Q. nit vorbey gehen, welcher, ob er gleich nit gedop-pelt wird in einem Wort, so man ansicht, wie dasselbe geschriben wird, nihilominus in istis vocibus, nichts desto weniger in denen Wörtern, Acqua, aqua, Wasser, acque die Wasser, item giacqui, jacui, ich bin gelegen, giacque . jacuit, er ist gelegen, giacquero, jacuerunt, sie seynd ge-legen; Et modo consimili, de cateris, qua habent C. ante Q. in istis inquam, item videtur prorsus, esse, in proferendo sonus, ac si geminunt haberent, Q. Vnd gleicher weise von den andern, welche ein C. vor dem Q. haben, in denen sprich ich, schei-net gleichmässiger Hall im außsprechen zuseyn, als ob ob sie zwey Q. hätten. Idem
units.tr: And in those that are compounded with Ra, as rapporto, I bring, refero; rapello, I withdraw, renoco; and finally in the word oppongo, oppono, I set against, C.p.pongo. Nor will I pass over the letter Q, which, though it is not doubled in any word as it is seen written, nevertheless in these words, acqua, aqua, water; acque, the waters; item giacqui, jacui, I have lain; giacque, jacuit, he has lain; giacquero, jacuerunt, they have lain; and in the same way with the others that have C before Q, in which, I say, there seems to be, in pronunciation, exactly the sound of a doubled Q.

units.la: Idem evenit de verbis, dißgeschicht auch in disen Worten; Nocqui, nocui, ich hab geschadet, nocque, nocuit, er hat geschadet, nocquero, nocuerunt, sie haben geschadet, deßgleichen mit nacqui, natus sum, ich bin geboren, nacque, natus est, er ist geboren, nacquero, nati sunt, sie seynd geboren. Idem placqui, placui, ich hab gefallen, placque, placuit, er hat gefallen, placquero, placuerunt, sie haben gefallen.
units.tr: The same happens with verbs, in these words: nocqui, nocui, I have harmed; nocque, nocuit, he has harmed; nocquero, nocuerunt, they have harmed; likewise with nacqui, natus sum, I was born; nacque, natus est, he was born; nacquero, nati sunt, they were born. Likewise placqui, placui, I have pleased; placque, placuit, he has pleased; placquero, placuerunt, they have pleased.

units.la: Item in verbis acquisto, acquiro, ich überkomme, vt & mi aueto, quiesco, ich gibe mich zu ruhe, cioe Io me acqueto, &c. R. & ipsum paßim reperitur in dictionibus geminatum. Es wird auch das R. in den Wörtern sehr offt gedoppelt funden, vt primum in verbis, quorum tertia persona sing. Num. praesent. indicativi definunt in Re, Als erstlich in denen Wörtern in der dritten Person, deß praesens indicat. sing. Num. so auff ein Re außgehen. Cuiusmodi sunt, als da seynd, Socorre, succurrit, er kömbt zuhülff, abhorre, abhorret, er abscheuet, hat ein abscheu, corre, currit, er lauffet, excipitur more, moritur, er stirbt. Geminatur praeterea in verbis, e quorum medio per elegantiam sermonis auferuntur Syllabae ne, & glie, quae pracedebant literam R. & adjungitur alterum R. Vber daß wird es in denen verbis gedoppelt, in welchen wegen der Zierligkeit im reden die Sylben ne vnd glie, so vor dem Buchstaben R, vorher giengen, werden außgeworffen, vnnd daßdarfür ein ander R.hinein gesetzt, Also daß man vor tenero sagt, terro, als io tenero, io terro, tenebo, ich werde halten, vnd auß veniro, wird verro, veniam, io verro, ich werd kommen, Also ex cogliero fit corro, colligam, ich werd zusamen lesen, cogliere, corre, colligere, zusamen lesen, auffsamlen, Item venirei, verrei venirem, daß ich doch käme, daß ich wurde kommen.
units.tr: Likewise in the verbs acquisto, acquiro, I obtain; and also mi aueto, quiesco, I give myself rest, that is, Io me acqueto, etc. R. is also found doubled in many words. It is found doubled very often in words, first in verbs whose third person singular of the present indicative ends in Re: as socorre, succurrit, he comes to help; abhorre, abhorret, he abhors, he has an aversion; corre, currit, he runs; excipitur more, moritur, he dies. It is further doubled in verbs from which, for elegance of speech, the syllables ne and glie, which came before the letter R, are removed, and another R is added in their place. So before tenero one says terro, as io tenero, io terro; tenebo, I shall hold; and from veniro comes verro, veniam, io verro, I shall come. Thus ex cogliero becomes corro, colligam, I shall gather together; cogliere, corre, colligere, to gather together, to collect. Likewise venirei, verrei, venirem, that I might come, that I would come.

units.la: Item geminatur in vocibus, Es wird auch in denen Wörtern gedoppelt, als Carro, Currus, Wagen, Torre, Turris, Thurn, Terra, die Erde, Arra, Maälschatz, quae sunt nomina, welches Namen sind, vnd in denen Wörtern oder verbis, Narro, ich erzehle, Atterro, ad terram dejcio, ich wirff zu Boden, ferro, claudo, ich verspperre, ich verschliesse, afferro, aripio, ich ergreiffe mit Gewalt, Sotterro, terram operio, ich decke mit Erden zu, ich begrab.
units.tr: Likewise it is doubled in words: as carro, currus, wagon; torre, turris, tower; terra, earth; arra, pledge, earnest money, which are nouns; and in words or verbs: narro, I relate; atterro, ad terram dejicio, I throw to the ground; ferro, claudo, I bar, I shut; afferro, aripio, I seize by force; sotterro, terram operio, I cover with earth, I bury.

units.la: Postremo, in verbis compositis, ex praepositione ad, Letzlich in den Wörtern, so mit der praepositione ad, seynd zusamen gesetzt: seyn, Arrestarsi, innstehen, stillstehen, stillhalten, item arrischio, periculum subeo, ich komm in Gefahr, Arrivo, advenio, ich gelang an, Arricchire & arrichire, ditare, bereicheren, bereichen, Arrostisco, torreo, ich brate, Nec S. non geminatur, quando quidem dicamus. Nicht weniger S. wird auch gedoppelt, dann wir sagen, Cassa, Arca, Truhe oder Kasten, Kiste, Ossa, fossa, Bein, Gruben, fouea, sunt & verba, verba, seyn auch etliche Wörter, als ich kan, poffo, poffum, Arroffifco, ich wird schamroth, erubesco, &c.
units.tr: Lastly, in verbs compounded with the preposition ad: arrestarsi, to stand in, to stand still, to hold still; likewise arrischio, periculum subeo, I run into danger; arrivo, advenio, I arrive; arricchire and arrichire, ditare, to enrich; arrostisco, torreo, I roast. Nor is S. doubled less, since we say cassa, arca, chest, box or coffer; ossa, fossa, bone, pit, fouea, ditch. There are also verbs: as I can, poffo, poffum; arroffifco, I blush, erubesco, etc.

units.la: S. praeterea geminatur, in iis nominibus, quae a latinis vocibus deducuntur, habentibus literam X.
units.tr: S. is further doubled in those nouns which are derived from Latin words having the letter X.

units.la: Vber daß wird S. gedoppelt, in denen Wörtern, so vom Lateinischen herkommen, vnd welche ein X. haben, als auß Saxum wird Saffo, ein Stein, ex Luxuria, Luffuria, Gailheit, Fixus, affixus, angehefft, angeschlagen, angestecht, fiffo, affiffo, idem fitto, pro Alexander, Alessandro, vor dixit, diffe, er hat gesagt, vixi, vissi, ich hab gelebt, Rexi, rexi, ich hab regiert, texo, teffo, ich web, wircke, Leinwath.
units.tr: Furthermore, S is doubled in words that come from Latin and have an X: from Saxum comes Saffo, a stone; from Luxuria, Luffuria, lust; Fixus, affixus, fastened, affixed, fixed; fiffo, affiffo, idem fitto; for Alexander, Alessandro; for dixit, diffe, he has said; vixi, vissi, I have lived; rexi, rexi, I have ruled; texo, teffo, I weave, I work linen.

units.la: Item fit in nominibus, quae a Latinis veniunt, habentibus P. ante S. Eben difes findt auch statt, in denen Wörtern, die vom Lateinischen, so vor dem S, ein P. haben, herkommen, als pro ipse dicamus Effo, derselbe, pro Gypsum Geffo, Gips, profcripfit, fcriffe, er hat geschriben, Verum retinetur P. in iis nominibus propriis. Iedoch wird das P. behalten, in difen eigenen Namen. Ipfi file, Ipfieratia, & capfa, einer Statt eigener Nam, atque illudobiter annotabo, P. auferri, cum praecedit literam S, in principio dictionis, relicta ipsa litera S.
units.tr: The same happens in nouns that come from Latin and have P before S. For instance, we say Effo, that same, for pro ipse dicamus; Geffo, gypsum, for Gypsum; profcripfit, fcriffe, he has written. However P is retained in these proper names: Ipfi file, Ipfieratia, and capfa, the proper names of a city. And I will note briefly that P is dropped when it stands before the letter S at the beginning of a word, leaving the S alone.

units.la: Vnd das will ich auch mit wenigem melden, daß das P. wird weggeworffen, wann es vor dem Buchstaben S, stehet, zu anfang eines Worts, vnd bleibet das S. nur allein, vt dicimus, als wir sagen, Salmo, vor Psalmus, &c. Proinde geminatur in vocibus, quae a Latinis veniunt, habentibus P. ante S. Ferner wird es gedoppelt, in disen Wörtern, welche von dem Lateinischen, so ein P. vor dem S. haben, herkommen, vt sunt, welche da seyn, Absoluto ex absolutus, auffgelöst, entbunden, Absorto ex absorptus, verschluckt, verschlungen, Absente ex absens, abwesend, Absentio ex absentimus, Wassertrüncker, Absentio, absynthium; Wermut Kraut.
units.tr: I will also note briefly that P is dropped when it stands before S at the beginning of a word, the S alone remaining, as we say Salmo for Psalmus, etc. Accordingly S is doubled in words that come from Latin with P before S, as these: absoluto from absolutus, released, freed; absorto from absorptus, swallowed up; absente from absens, absent; absentio from absentimus, a water-drinker; absentio, absynthium, wormwood herb.

units.la: Geminatur item in ultima Syllaba praeterito imperf. vt mehr wird es gedoppelt in der letzten Sylben deß imperf. Optatiui Num. sing. als Amaffi, amarem, daß ich solt lieben, amaffe, amaret, daß er solt lieben, und also auch in dergleichen Coniugationen zuverfahren.
units.tr: It is further doubled in the last syllable of the imperfect optative, as in the singular: Amaffi, amarem, that I should love; amaffe, amaret, that he should love; and proceed in the same way in such conjugations.

units.la: Cum vero Num. est plur. in media Syllaba, vt, &c. wenn es aber plur. Num. ist, wird S. in der mitleren Sylben gedoppelt, als amaffimo, amaremus, daß wir solten lieben, amaffero, amarent, daß sie solten lieben. Item in denen praeteritis indicatiuis, deren verborum, so tertia Coniugationis seynd, gleichfals das S. zudoppeln, als percossi, percussi, percoffe, percussit, ich hab geschlagen, er hat geschlagen, percoffero, percusserunt, sie haben geschlagen; Item in verbis Compositis, ex praepositione ad, da finden sich widerumb, Affaggio, zufio, ich versuch, ich kostes, die Speiß oder
units.tr: When the number is plural, S is doubled in the middle syllable, as amaffimo, amaremus, that we should love; amaffero, amarent, that they should love. Likewise in the perfect indicatives of those verbs that belong to the third conjugation, S is likewise doubled: percossi, percussi, percoffe, percussit, I have struck, he has struck; percoffero, percusserunt, they have struck. Likewise in compound verbs with the preposition ad there are again found: Affaggio, zufio, I try, I taste the food or

units.la: Tranck. Affalto, adorior, ich falle an, Afficuro, ich verficher, tutum reddo, assegno, assigno, ich zeichne zu, ich zeichne an, Affordo, furdum reddo, ich mache taub, affomiglio, assimilo, ich vergleiche zu etwas, dicimus, wir sagen, raffumo, veliterum fumo, ich nimb es wider, Item raffetto, concinno, ich richte schön zusammen. Quod autem spectat ad literam T. was aber den Buchstaben T. belangt, reperitur & ipsa geminata in iis nempe vocibus, quæ veniunt à latinis habentibus B. aut C. aut P. ante T. Wird auch diser gedoppelt gefunden in denen Wörtern, welche herkommen von den Lateinischen, so ein B. ein C. oder ein P. vor dem T. haben.
units.tr: drink. Affalto, adorior, I attack; Afficuro, I assure, tutum reddo; assegno, assigno, I assign, I mark out; Affordo, furdum reddo, I make deaf; affomiglio, assimilo, I compare to something; we say raffumo, veluti iterum fumo, I take it up again; likewise raffetto, concinno, I arrange neatly together. As for the letter T, it too is found doubled in those words which come from Latin having B, C or P before T.

units.la: Hinc fit, vt pro obtusus dicamus ottusfo, stumpff, vor obtineo, ottengo, ich erhalt, ich erlang, vor otto, otto, acht, achte die Zahl, pro doctus, dotto, gelehrt, profactus, fatto, gemacht, gethan, pro Baptismus, Battesimo, Tauff, pro septem, sette, siben, pro ruptus, rotto, zerbrochen, vnd vor corruptus, corotto, verderbt.
units.tr: Hence it comes about that for obtusus we say ottusfo, blunt; for obtineo, ottengo, I obtain, I attain; for otto, otto, eight, the number eight; for doctus, dotto, learned; for factus, fatto, made, done; for Baptismus, Battesimo, baptism; for septem, sette, seven; for ruptus, rotto, broken; and for corruptus, corotto, corrupted.

units.la: Petrarcha tamen scripsit, rapto raptus, quo poneret discrimen inter hoc rapienti nomen, & Adverbium ratto, velociter.
units.tr: Petrarch, however, wrote rapto for raptus, so as to distinguish this word for seizing from the adverb ratto, quickly.

units.la: Petrarcha aber hat rapto geschriben, damit er einen vnderschid machte, vnder difem Wort, das rauben oder nemmen heißt, vnd vnder dem Adverbio ratto, welches geschwinde heißt.
units.tr: Petrarch, however, wrote rapto, so that he would make a distinction between this word, which means to seize or take, and the adverb ratto, which means quickly.

units.la: Geminatur rursum in iis diminutivis vocibus. Widerumb wird das T. auch gedoppelt, in denen Wörtern, welches diminutiva seyn, als pauperculus, armer elender Mann; Libretto, Libellus, Büchlein; Fanciulletto, puerulus, Knäblein; Boschetto, parvum Nemus, kleines Gebüsch, Wäldlein.
units.tr: The T is also doubled again in diminutive words, such as pauperculus, a poor wretched man; Libretto, Libellus, a little book; Fanciulletto, puerulus, a little boy; Boschetto, parvum nemus, a small grove, a little wood.

units.la: Demum in verbis compositis, ex praepositione ad, Letzlich in den Wörtern, so der praepositio ad seyn zusammengesetzt, wird das T gedoppelt, als Attrisio, triftor, ich betrübe, mache bekümmert; Attero, ich wirff zu Boden; adterram deicio.
units.tr: Lastly, the T is doubled in compound words formed with the preposition ad, such as Attrisio, triftor, I grieve, I make sorrowful; Attero, I throw to the ground; adterram deicio.

units.la: Das V. aber wird doppelt gefunden, in denen Wörtern, V. autem duplicatur in verbis, Annen-tarsi, irruere, vngestümmig angehen, Auuertire, animadvertere, vermahnen, Auuotarsi, vouere, sich verloben, Gelübd thun.
units.tr: The V, however, is found doubled in words such as Annen-tarsi, irruere, to attack impetuously; Auuertire, animadvertere, to admonish; Auuotarsi, vouere, to pledge oneself, to make a vow.

units.la: Attamen scribendum est, Auenire, & non annuenire, ut nonnullis placet. Doch muß man schreiben, Auenire, sich begeben, fürfallen, vnd nicht annuenire, wie etliche wollen. Propterea quod annuenire non ex verbo latino advenio, quod pervenio declarat, derivatur. Dieweil das Wort annuenire nicht von dem Lateinischen advenio, welches heißt, ich komme hinzu, herkömbt, sed a verbo evenit, quod est accidit, quae significatio verbo plane convenit. Sondern von dem verbo Evenit, welches heißt, es gefchicht, es begibt sich, welche bedeutung mit dem verbo Auenire gantz überein kömbt. Cate-
units.tr: Still, one must write Auenire, to happen, to befall, and not annuenire, as some prefer. For the word annuenire is not derived from the Latin advenio, which means to come to, but from the verb evenit, which means it happens, it comes about, and that meaning agrees entirely with the word Auenire. Cate-

units.la: Caeterum de literis X. Y. & K. illud ignorare non oportet, Ferner ist von denen Buchstaben X. Y. vnd K. difes zuwissen, Nullius fane vsus esse apud Italos homines, daß sie bey den Italiänern keinen nutzen haben, Ob id eas inter cateras literas non connumerauimus, welche sie deßwegen nicht vnder die andern Buchstaben zehlen.
units.tr: Moreover, concerning the letters X, Y and K, one must know this: they have no use at all among Italian people, and for that reason we have not counted them among the other letters.

units.la: Nam pro Y. vtuntur I. pro K. C. & loco literae X. vtuntur S. Denn vor das Y. gebrauchen sie ein I. für das K. ein C. vnd an statt deß X. brauchen sie ein S. vt supra ostendimus, wie oben angezeigt, Aut geminatum in media scilicet distione, aut simplex in media item distione aliquando. Oder machen das S. doppelt, im mitten deß Worts, oder nur einfach, auch bißweiln in der mitten, & semper in eiusdem principio, allezeit zu anfang deßelben. Atque quod ad principium attinet, dicimus. Darumb sagen wir zu anfang deß Worts, Senocrate, pro Xenocrates, & Senofonte pro Xenophon, Serse pro Xerxes.
units.tr: For in place of Y they use I, in place of K they use C, and in place of the letter X they use S, as we showed above, either doubled in the middle of a word, or single in the middle of a word at times, and always at the beginning of the same word. And as regards the beginning of a word, we say: Senocrate for Xenocrates, and Senofonte for Xenophon, Serse for Xerxes.

units.la: Postremum Litera Z. quae postrema est omnium literarum, quibus Itali vntur, duplicatur & ipsa cum interponitur inter duas vocales.
units.tr: The last letter, Z, which is the final one of all the letters the Italians use, is also doubled when it is placed between two vowels.

units.la: Letstlich wird auch das Z. so der letste Buchstaben vnder allen ist, welche die Welschen gebrauchen, wird gedoppelt, wenn es zwischen zwene selb lautende Buchstaben gesetzt wird, als in Bellezza, Dolcezza, Gentilezza, Schönheit, Süeßigkeit, Höfligkeit. Cum vero praeceditur a confonanti aliqua, simplex reponitur, wann aber ein mitlautender vorher gehet, wird nur ein einiges gesetzt, als in Speranza, Hoffnung, Partenza, Abreisung, Licenza, Abdanckung, Beurlaubung, Sapienza, Weisheit. Sed illud est hic observandum Z. non recte geminari in voce Me-zo. Dises aber ist hier zumercken, daß das Z. nicht recht gedoppelt wird, in dem Wort Me-zo, quanquam utrimq; vocalem habeat, ob es gleich vor sich vnd nach sich, einen vocalem hat, nec obstat, quod Petrarcha secus fecerit, vnd hindert nicht, daß Petrarcha anders geschriben.
units.tr: Lastly, the Z, which is the last of all the letters the Italians use, is also doubled when it is set between two vowels, as in Bellezza, Dolcezza, Gentilezza: beauty, sweetness, courtesy. When, however, a consonant comes before it, only a single one is put, as in Speranza, hope; Partenza, departure; Licenza, dismissal, leave-taking; Sapienza, wisdom. But here it must be noted that Z is not rightly doubled in the word Me-zo, although it has a vowel on both sides, and it does not hinder that Petrarch wrote otherwise.

units.la: Quandoquidem fuit ad id necessitate illarum pro-tremarum vocum in Carmine, quas Rimas appel-lamus, adduxit. Sintemal er auß noth derselben Sylben in Versen, die wir Reimen nennen, dißzuthun gezwungen worden. Nam cum pronun-ciamus Mezo, dann wann wir außsprechen Mezo, mittel, mitten, liquido apparet, (modo quis Italice pronunciandi rationem teneat) non perinde pronunciare ac pezzo, frustrum, &c. so sihet ein jeder, der nur Italiänisch weiß außzusprechen, daß man nicht sage, als wie Pezzo, ein Stück, Auezzo, affuetus, gewehnt, vnd dergleichen mehr.
units.tr: Since it was by necessity of those double-sounded syllables in verse, which we call rhymes, that he was compelled to do this. For when we pronounce Mezo, middle, in the middle, it is plain (provided one knows the manner of Italian pronunciation) that we do not pronounce it in the same way as pezzo, a piece, Auezzo, accustomed, and the like: anyone who knows how to pronounce Italian sees that one does not say it as one says Pezzo, a piece, Auezzo, accustomed, and suchlike.

units.la: Et quoniam aliquando non solum similes Consonantes duplicantur in dictione, sed etiam diuerfæ. Vnd weil bißweilen nicht nur allein gleiche Consonantes werden in einem Wort gedoppelt, sondern dern auch vngleiche; Atq; non modo duplicantur, verum triplices reperiuntur quoque, Vnnd nicht nur allein gedoppelte, sondern wol dreyfache gefunden werden.
units.tr: And since sometimes not only like consonants are doubled within a word, but also unlike ones. And not only are doubled consonants found, but indeed triple ones are found as well.

units.la: Ideo huius rei rationem declarare, Opera precium esse iudico, Als sihet michs vor nothwendig an, deßen vrsach zuerklæren. Illud itaque principio in hac testatur. Ist derowegen anfangs difes zumercken.
units.tr: I therefore think it worth the effort to explain the reason for this matter. So first of all this is to be noted in this regard.

units.la: Non pati fermonem Italicum, ut suis dictionibus duæ similes Consonantes præponantur, Daß die welsche Sprach nicht könne dulden, daß man jhren Wörtern zwene gleiche Consonantes vorsetze, Etenim si quis ita scriberet, Denn so jemand also wolte schreiben, Ssoperbo, Vvenere, id non Italice faceret, der handelte wider die Welsche Sprach, es wäre gar nit Italienisch, Atqui nihil prohibet, Nichts aber hindert, quo minus duæ Consonantes diuersæ nonnullis dictionibus præponi possint, Daß man zwene vngleiche Consonantes, etliche Wörtern könne vorsetzen, vt videre est, wie zusehen ist, in spero, studio, scarico, credo, prezzo, ich hoff, befleißige, entledige, glaube, der Werth. Quinimo tres quoque interdum ita dictionibus Italicis præposita reperiuntur, Ja man findet, daß auch manchmahl drey in Italienischen Wörtern vorgesetzt werden: Als Strada, via, Weeg, strale, sagitta, Pfeyl, Stratagema, Kriegeslist, strano, frembd, Stretto, eng, zusam gestrengt, stringo
units.tr: The Italian language does not allow two like consonants to be placed before a word, for if anyone wrote thus, Ssoperbo, Vvenere, he would not be writing Italian, yet nothing prevents two unlike consonants from being placed before some words, as can be seen in spero, studio, scarico, credo, prezzo: I hope, I study, I unload, I believe, the price. Indeed, three are also sometimes found placed before Italian words in this way: Strada, via, way; strale, sagitta, arrow; Stratagema, stratagem; strano, strange; Stretto, narrow, pressed together; stringo,

units.la: ich ftreng zufam, fprezzo, ich veracht, sperno, splendore, Glantz, splendido, glantzend, herr- lich, &c.
units.tr: I press tightly together; sprezzo, I despise; sperno; splendore, splendour; splendido, splendid, glorious, etc.

units.la: Proinde in medio dictionis, haud possunt tres diuerfæ Confonantes poni. Aber in der mitten eines Worts, können drey Confonanten gar nicht beyfamen ftehen, idcirco non dicimus, drumb fagen wir nicht, Conftante, transformo, transmuto, obstacolo, fobstegno, postposito; fondern wir fagen im Welfchen, Costante, beftåndig, trasformo, ich vergeftalte, trasmuto, ich veråndere, Ostacolo, Hindernuß, Sostegno, Vnderftütz, postposto, hindan gefetzt, Excipiuntur, werden außgenommen, Moftro, ich zeige, weife, sempre, allezeit, Sepolcro, Grab, Abbreuio, ich verkürtze, accresco, ich vermehre, oder nimm zu, attrauerfo, vber zwerch.
units.tr: Therefore, in the middle of a word, three different consonants cannot be placed together, so we do not say Constante, transformo, transmuto, obstacolo, fobstegno, postposito; rather, in Italian we say Costante, constant; trasformo, I transform; trasmuto, I change; Ostacolo, obstacle; Sostegno, support; postposto, placed behind. Exceptions are made for Mostro, I show, point out; sempre, always; Sepolcro, grave; Abbreuio, I abbreviate; accresco, I increase, or I grow; attrauerso, crosswise.

units.la: Porro de H. aspirationis nota, vsu illud ignorare minime debes, Vber daß follman difes von dem Buchftaben H. welcher ein Merckzeichen einer anhauchung ift, nicht auß der acht zulaffen, Nempe folere a plerisque Italicis Scriptoribus pont in omnibus fere illis dictionibus, quas a Latinis accepimus, Nemlich, daß die meiften Italienifchen Scribenten, daffelbige H. faft in allen Wörtern pflegen zufetzen, die wir von den Lateinern bekommen, Et in quibus ipsi Latini aspiratione sunt vsi, Vnd in welcher die Lateiner die anhauchung gebrauchet haben, Als in Huomo ex homo
units.tr: Furthermore, concerning the sign of aspiration, the H, you must by no means ignore its use: namely, that most Italian writers are accustomed to put this H in almost all those words which we have taken from the Latins, and in which the Latins themselves used aspiration, as in Huomo from homo

units.la: Mensch, Humano ex humanus, Menschlich, freundtlich, Ho ex habeo, ich hab, &c.
units.tr: Man, humano from humanus; human, friendly; ho from habeo, I have; etc.

units.la: Atqui ablata cum fit nostra atate causa, weil aber zu difer vnserer Zeit, die vrsach ist auffgehoben. Cur aspirationis nota est quasitus vsus, cessare quidem, vt opinor, debere videretur effectus, Warumb man die anhauchung erfunden, als solte zwar meinem bedüncken nach, der Effect auch aufthören.
units.tr: But since in our age the reason for it has been removed, the cause is taken away. Why the use of the aspiration mark was sought, the effect, I think, ought seemingly to cease as well. (German: since in our time the cause of it is removed; why the aspiration mark was invented, the effect should in my opinion cease as well.)

units.la: Hoc est, vt H. pro signo crassioris Spiritus, (quomodo admodum paucas pronunciamus) in Italicis vocibus amplius nonponeretur, Das ist, das H. solte in denen Italienischen Wörtern, für ein Zeichen eines härtern vnd gröbern lauts, (wie wir sehr wenig aussprechen,) nicht mehr gebraucht werden, Sed tamen huius aspirationis vsus in pauca mihi videtur esse contrahendus, Aber mich bedünckt, der gebrauch difer anhauchung, soll kurtz zusamen gezogen werden, vt quidem primum retineatur in voce huomo ad tegandam scilicet turpitudinem illam, Also daß er erstlichen zwar behalten werde, in dem Wort huomo, damit man ein wenig bedecke den vnfreundtlichen Hall, qua huic nomini provenire videtur, ex diphthongo VO, so difern Wort herzukommen scheinet, von dem Diphthongo VO, quasi in Capite huius distionis collocata, so zu anfangs gleich stehet.
units.tr: That is, that H, as a sign of a harder and rougher sound (which we pronounce very seldom), should no longer be used in Italian words. (German: that H, as a sign of a harder and coarser sound, which we pronounce very seldom, should no longer be used in Italian words.) But nevertheless, it seems to me that the use of this aspiration should be cut back to a few cases. (German: but it seems to me that the use of this aspiration should be narrowed down.) So that it is first retained in the word huomo, namely to cover up that unpleasant rasp, which seems to arise in this noun from the diphthong VO, placed at the very beginning of the word. (German: so that first it is kept in the word huomo, to soften that unfriendly breathing, which seems to come to this word from the diphthong VO, standing at the head of the word.)

units.la: Deinde ne amoueatur ex verbo ho, id est habeo, ich habe, darnach soll es nit verworffen werden im verbo.
units.tr: Next, it should not be removed from the verb ho, that is, I have. (German: nor should it be dropped in the verb ho, I have.)

units.la: im verbo ho, ieh hab, Idque ad differentiam conjii-tuendam, inter ipsum Ho, & O, Adverbium vocandi, atque O, distungendi particulam, vnd solches darumb,damit ein vnderscheid bleibe,zwischen dem verbo Ho, vnd O, welches eine Coniunctio disjunctiua, vnd zwischen dem O, welches ein Adverbium vocandi ist.
units.tr: In the verb ho, I have. And this is to keep a distinction between the verb Ho and O, the adverb of calling, and between O, the disjunctive conjunction.

units.la: Item inter Ha, habet, er hat, & A, praepositio-nem, datiuo casui seruientem, Item vnder dem Ha, vnd A, so eine praepofition ist, vnd dem datiuo dienet.
units.tr: Likewise, between Ha, he has, and A, the preposition serving the dative case, the same distinction should be kept.

units.la: Postremum vt conseruetur in iftis syllabis, Che, Chi, Ghe, Ghi, Letzlich soll es auch behalten werden, in denen Sylben Che, Chi, Ghe, Ghi, in quibus reuera signum est, Spiritus crassioris, da es ein recht Zeichen ist, einer härtern anhauchung, quo hae syllabae ab illis differant, damit die Sylben von denen vnderschiden werden können, quae habent ce, ci, ge, gi, so da seynd ce, ci, ge, gi, Nam quantum interfit vero modo pronuncies, illi recte norunt, qui Italicè pronunciandi tenent rationem, Denn wie groffes dran gelegen fey, ob man so oder so ausspreche, wissen die jenigen am besten, denen die Manier Italienisch zureden bekandt ist.
units.tr: Lastly, it should be kept in these syllables, Che, Chi, Ghe, Ghi, in which it is truly a sign of a harder aspiration, by which these syllables are distinguished from those which have ce, ci, ge, gi. For those who know the rules of speaking Italian know best how much it matters whether one pronounces it this way or that.

units.la: Quod autem ad vocales attinet, illud sciendum est, eas coalescere, in diphthongos, quae sunt AV, Aura, Laura, Maura, Was aber die Vocales belangt, so ist zuwissen, daß diefelben zusammen gefügt werden. fügt werden, in die diphthongen, welche haben im außreden AV, als Aura, sanffte Lufft, Laura, Maura, eigene Namen, Eu, Euro, Ostwind, Sceuro.
units.tr: As for the vowels, it must be understood that they combine into diphthongs, which in pronunciation are AU: Aura, Laura, Maura, gentle breeze, proper names; EU: Euro, the east wind; Sceuro.

units.la: IE, vieni, kom, Brieue, kurtz, Tiene, tenet, es hält, Ieri, heri, geftern, pieno, plenus, voll, völlig, Fieno, fœnum, Heu, Ia, ciancire, garrire, Wäscherey treiben, Ciance, Nuga, Narrenposs- sen, Bianco, albus, weiß, Caccia, Venatio, Jagt.
units.tr: IE: vieni, come; brieue, short; tiene, tenet, he holds; ieri, heri, yesterday; pieno, plenus, full, complete; fieno, fœnum, hay; IA: ciancire, garrire, to chatter, to babble; ciance, nuga, silly nonsense; bianco, albus, white; caccia, venatio, hunt.

units.la: IO, Fiore, flos, Blum, Sciocco, ineptus, vngeschickt, scioglio, foluo, ich löse auff, Scioperato, Ceffator, Otiosus, müßig, Müßiggänger, IV, Ciurma, Turma, ein Hauffen, Schiuma, Spuma, Schaum, più, plus, mehr, Giù, deorsum, vnderfich, niderwarts.
units.tr: IO: fiore, flos, flower; sciocco, ineptus, unskilled, foolish; scioglio, soluo, I loosen, I dissolve; scioperato, cessator, otiosus, idle, a loafer; IU: ciurma, turma, a crowd; schiuma, spuma, foam; piu, plus, more; giu, deorsum, down, downwards.

units.la: IVO, Figliuolo, Filius, Sohn, Giuoco, iocus, Scherz, Spil, ludus, VO, Huomo, homo, Menfch, Vópo, Opus, Werck, Vouo, Ouum, Eyer, Buono, bonus, gut, Cuoco, Cocus, Koch, VI, Guida, Dux, Führer, Leiter, Piacqui, placui, Ich hab gefallen. Acquisto, acquiro, ich überkomm, erlang, quinto, der fünffte. VE, Piacque, placuit, es hat jhm gefallen. Acque, aqua, die Waffer. Adunque, igitur, derhalben, Lingue, die Zungen. VA, Acqua, aqua, Waffer, Lingua, Zunge, Guadagno, lucrum, Gewin. Fernet in AI, Fai, facis, du thuft, fai, fas, du stehest, Amai, amasti, ich hab geliebt, Lai, Lamentationes, Klagungen, Leid, farai, facies, du wirft thun, VAI. Guai, va, vel aruumna, wehe, Wehmütigkeit. IEI, miei, mei, meine.
units.tr: IUO: figliuolo, filius, son; giuoco, iocus, jest, play, ludus; VO: huomo, homo, man; vopo, opus, work; vouo, ouum, egg; buono, bonus, good; cuoco, cocus, cook; VI: guida, dux, leader, guide; piacqui, placui, I have pleased; acquisto, acquiro, I acquire, I obtain; quinto, the fifth. VE: piacque, placuit, it has pleased him; acque, aqua, waters; adunque, igitur, therefore; lingue, tongues. VA: acqua, aqua, water; lingua, tongue; guadagno, lucrum, gain. Further, in AI: fai, facis, you do; fai, fas, you stand; amai, amasti, I have loved; lai, lamentationes, laments, sorrows; farai, facies, you will do. VAI: guai, va, vel aruumna, woe, lamentation. IEI: miei, mei, my.

units.la: Ei. Lei, ea, fie, Coffei, hæc, die, fie, diefelbe, fey, es, du bift, Vos. tuoi, tui, deine, fuoi, fui, feine, Buoi, Bouet, Rinder, & vnoi, vis, wiltu.
units.tr: Ei; lei, ea, she; caffei, haec, these; fie, be, she is, it is, you are; vostri, tuoi, tui, your; suoi, sui, his; buoi, boves, oxen; and vnoi, vis, will you?

units.la: Hic animadvertas licet, Hiebey ist zumer-eken, daß Tuo, Suo, Io, Lei, Lui, Noi, vos, Tuoi, dein seyn, ich, sie, er, wir, ihr, deine, &c. plerumque monosyllaba esse, tum in profa ratione, tum in versu, gemeinglich eintylbige Wörter seyn, so wol auffer, als in den Versen, Quanquam quod ad versum spectat, in fine Carminis semper diffyllaba sunt, Wiewol sie, was den Vers belanget, im ende allezeit zweyfylbig seynd.
units.tr: Here it may be noted that tuo, suo, io, lei, lui, noi, vos, tuoi, dein (your), I, she, he, we, you, your and so on are generally monosyllables, both in prose and in verse. Yet as far as verse is concerned, they are always disyllables at the end of a line.

units.la: Neque praetermiserim quo ad pronunciationem Vocalium illud esse observandum; Dises ist auch nicht zuverschweigen, daß man in außspre-chung der selbstlautenden Buchstaben merecke. O & E, aliquando obscurius, aliquando clarius pronunciari, Wie das O vnd E, zuweilen etwas gröber, zuweilen etwas heller außgesprochen werde. Obscurius enim ipsa dictionibus, Gröber in disen Wörtern, Amore, Lieb, Calore, Hitz, Ardore, Brunst, vnd dergleichen. At clarius pronunciatur E, in dictione Erba. O, vero, in dictione Ottima, Aber das E, wird heller außgesprochen in dem Wort Erba, Kraut, vnd das O, in dem Wort Ottima, die allerbeste.
units.tr: Nor should it be passed over that in pronouncing the vowels one must observe this: the O and E are sometimes pronounced more heavily, sometimes more clearly. The O and E are heavier in such words as amore, love; calore, heat; ardore, ardour, and similar words. But E is pronounced more clearly in the word erba, herb, and O in the word ottima, the very best.

units.la: Verum hac pronunciandi ratio, haud scripto effendi potest. Aber dise art außzusprechen, kan man im Buch nicht recht lehren, quare ab eo discendum. discenda omnino est, qui Italicam linguam callet, ist derowegen von einem zulehrnen, der die Welsche Sprache kan, vnd versehet.
units.tr: Yet this manner of pronunciation cannot be taught properly in a book. It must therefore be learned from one who knows the Italian language thoroughly and has mastered it.

units.la: DE ARTICVLIS.
units.tr: ON THE ARTICLES.

units.la: Von den Geschlechts Wörtlein.
units.tr: Of the Gender-Words.

units.la: HAbet sermo Italicus articulos, quos nominibus quae propria non sunt, praeponit.
units.tr: The Italian language has articles, which it places before nouns that are not proper.

units.la: Die Welsche Sprach hat gewisse Geschlechts Wörtlein, so sie denen Wörtlein vorsetzet, welche nicht propria seynd.
units.tr: The Italian language has certain gender-words, which it places before words that are not proper nouns.
