units.la: Quorum alij viriles sunt, alij muliebres. Deren seynd etliche Mannliche, etliche Weibliche. Idque tam in singulari, quam in multitudinis numero, vt hic subiectus Typus clare ostendit. Sowol in singulari, als plurali numero, wie dise beygesetzte Tafel klärlich aufweiset. Viriles, Num. sing. il, lo, der, hic. Mannliche. Num. plur. i, li, gli, die, lat. hi Muliebres, Num. sing. La, die, hac. Weibliche. Num. plur. Le, die, Lat. ha.
units.tr: Of these, some are masculine and others feminine. Of these there are some masculine and some feminine. And this holds in the singular as well as in the plural number, as the table set out here clearly shows. In the singular as well as the plural number, as the table added here shows clearly. Masculine, singular: il, lo, der, this. Masculine, plural: i, li, gli, die, these. Feminine, singular: La, die, this. Feminine, plural: Le, die, these.

units.la: Caret Italicus Sermo Casibus. Die Welsche Sprach hat keine Casus, qua quidem in re, vt est simüis Ling. Hebraica, in welchem, gleich wie sie mit der Hebreischen Sprach überein kömbt; Ita est Graeca & Latina dissimilis. Also ist sie der Griechischen vnd Lateinischen gantz vngleich.
units.tr: The Italian language has no cases. The Italian language has no cases. In this respect it agrees with the Hebrew language, but it is unlike Greek and Latin. So it is entirely unlike Greek and Latin.

units.la: Quapropter ad variandos Articulos per diuersos C
units.tr: Therefore, to vary the articles through the different

units.la: Casus adhibet praepositiones. Derowegen ge‑braucht sie praepositiones, die Artickel oder Ge‑schlechtswörter, durch die vnderschidliche Casus zuuerändern. DE. pro Genitiuo, vnd A. pro Dativo, & Da pro Ablatiuo, Innocatiuo vsurpatur pro Signo Casus, O. Aduerbium vocandi. Im Vocatiuo braucht man für deß Casus Merckzeichen, das Aduerbium vocandi, O.
units.tr: cases, it uses prepositions. Therefore it uses prepositions to vary the articles through the different cases. DE serves for the Genitive, A for the Dative, and DA for the Ablative. For the Vocative, O, the adverb of calling, is used as the sign of the case. In the Vocative one uses, as the mark of the case, the adverb of calling, O.

units.la: In Nominatiuo vero & Accusatiuo Articuli dumtaxat vsurpantur. Im Nominatiuo vnd Accusatiuo aber werden nur die Articul allein gebraucht, quemadmodum ex subiecto Typo, perspicipotest, wie auß vnderzeichneter Figur kan vnd mag gesehen werden.
units.tr: In the Nominative and Accusative, however, the articles alone are used. In the Nominative and Accusative, however, only the articles are used, as can be seen from the figure below, as may be seen from the figure printed underneath.

units.la: Nominatiuo. il, lo, der, hic.
units.tr: Nominative. il, lo, the, this.

units.la: Genitiuo. del, dello, huius, deß, dessen.
units.tr: Genitive. del, dello, of this, of the, of whom.

units.la: Dativo. al, allo, dem, deme, l. huic.
units.tr: Dative. al, allo, to the, to him, to this.

units.la: Accusatiuo. il, lo, der, hunc.
units.tr: Accusative. il, lo, the, this (acc.).

units.la: Vocatiuo. ó, O, O du.
units.tr: Vocative. ó, O, O you.

units.la: Ablatiuo. dal, dallo, ab hoc, von dem.
units.tr: Ablative. dal, dallo, from this, from the.

units.la: Nominatiuo. i, li, gli, die, hi, l.
units.tr: Nominative. i, li, gli, the, these.

units.la: Genitiuo. dei, de, delli & degli, deren, his.
units.tr: Genitive. dei, de, delli & degli, of the, of these.

units.la: Dativo ai, a, alli, denen, his.
units.tr: Dative. ai, a, alli, to the, to these.

units.la: Accusatiuo. i. li, gli, die, hos.
units.tr: Accusative. i, li, gli, the, these (acc.).

units.la: Vocatiuo. ó. O, O jhr.
units.tr: Vocative. ó, O, O you (plural).

units.la: Ablatiuo. dai, da, dalli & dagli, de his, von den.
units.tr: Ablative. dai, da, dalli & dagli, de his, from the.

units.la: Nominatiuo. La, die, hæc.
units.tr: Nominative. La, the, this (fem.).

units.la: Genitiuo. Dela vel della, der, huius.
units.tr: Genitive. Dela or della, of the, of this.

units.la: Datiuo. alla vel a la, der, huic.
units.tr: Dative. alla or a la, to the, to this.

units.la: Accusatiuo. La, die, hanc.
units.tr: Accusative. La, the, this (fem.).

units.la: Vocatiuo. O. O. O jhr.
units.tr: Vocative. O, O, O you (plural).

units.la: Ablatiuo. dalla vel dala, von der, abhac.
units.tr: Ablative. dalla or dala, from the, from this.

units.la: Nominatiu. Le, die, hæ.
units.tr: Nominative. Le, the, these (fem.).

units.la: Genitiuo. delle, vel dele, deren, harum.
units.tr: Genitive. delle or dele, of the, of these.

units.la: Datiuo. alle vel ale, denen, his.
units.tr: Dative. alle or ale, to the, to these.

units.la: Accusatiuo Le, die, has.
units.tr: Accusative. Le, the, these (fem.).

units.la: Vocatiuo. O. O, O jhr.
units.tr: Vocative. O, O, O you (plural).

units.la: Ablatiuo. dalle. oder da le, von den.
units.tr: Ablative. dalle or da le, from the.

units.la: Articuli conjuncti cum alijs Præpositionibus.
units.tr: Articles combined with other prepositions.

units.la: Nello, nel, in den.
units.tr: Nello, nel: in the.

units.la: Nelli, negli, nei ne, in denen.
units.tr: Nelli, negli, nei, ne: in those.

units.la: Nella, in der.
units.tr: Nella: in the.

units.la: Neile, in denen.
units.tr: Neile: in those.

units.la: Per lo, pel, pello, durch den,
units.tr: Per lo, pel, pello: through the.

units.la: Per li, pergli, pelli, per i, pei, pe, durch die.
units.tr: Per li, pergli, pelli, per i, pei, pe: through the.

units.la: Per la, durch die, durch sie.
units.tr: Per la: through the, through her.

units.la: Per le, durch die (Weiber) donne.)
units.tr: Per le: through the (women), donne.)

units.la: {Con} Con lo, col, coilo, mit dem, mit jhm.
units.tr: {Con} Con lo, col, coilo, with the, with him.

units.la: Con i, congli, colli, coi, co', mit jhnen, mit denen.
units.tr: Con i, congli, colli, coi, co', with them, with those.

units.la: Con la, colla, mit der.
units.tr: Con la, colla, with the.

units.la: Con le, colle, mit denen Töchtern,
units.tr: Con le, colle, with those daughters,

units.la: con le Figliuole.
units.tr: con le Figliuole. with the daughters.

units.la: DE ARTICVLORVM VSV.
units.tr: ON THE USE OF THE ARTICLES.

units.la: Von dem gebrauch der Geschlechtswörtlein.
units.tr: Of the use of the little gender words.

units.la: OMnes fere Articuli vocibus tantum communi-bus præponi solent. Es werden alle Articul faft nur zu denen nominibus appellativis gesetzt. Dixi fere, quod aliquando Articulus la, præponatur nominibus proprijs, ut suo loco demonstrabitur. Ich sage faft, dieweil zuweilen der Articul la, auch denen nominibus proprijs wird vorgesetzt, wie an seinem Orth soll erwisen werden. Articulus itaque Lo, datur vocibus incipientibus à vocali. Wird derowegen der Articul Lo, zu denen Wörtern gesetzt, die von einem Vocalen anfangen.
units.tr: Almost all articles are normally placed only before common nouns. Es werden alle Articul fast nur zu denen nominibus appellativis gesetzt. I say "almost", because sometimes the article la is also placed before proper nouns, as will be shown in its place. Therefore the article Lo is given to words beginning with a vowel.

units.la: Sed litera O. elidétur, appofita eius loco Apostropho, hoc modo, Aber der Buchstab O. wird ausgestossen, vnd stehet an seiner stell ein Apostrophus, oder ein Zeichen der hinweg werffung, auff solche gestalt, nemlich, L'amòre, L'onore, die Lieb,
units.tr: But the letter O is elided, and an apostrophe, or sign of omission, stands in its place, in this form: L'amore, L'onore, love, honour,

units.la: die Ehr, atq; perinde proferuntur, ac si scripta esf-sent, Iamore, lonore, vnd werden aufsgesprochen, als stünde geschriben, Lamore, lonore.
units.tr: the honour; and they are pronounced as if it were written, Lamore, lonore.

units.la: Sed hic animadvertendum est, Italos Hetuscros esse solitos auferre literam i, vocibus ijs, quae ex prae-positione In componuntur, atq; apponere Apostro-phum litera vocali articuli, Sic.
units.tr: But here it must be noted that the Tuscans, that is the Italians, are accustomed to drop the letter i from those words which are compounded with the preposition In, and to put an apostrophe after the vowel of the article, thus.

units.la: Hie aber ist zumercken, daß die Tuscaner pflegen den Buchstaben I. wegk zuwerffen, in denen Wörtern, welche mit der praepositiun In, zusammen gesetzt seynd, vnd einen Apostrophum zu den selbstlautenden Buchstaben deß Articuls zusetzen, als Lomperatore, der Keyser, in singulari, vnd in plurali, gli Imperatori, die Keyser, & ita de caeteris huiusmodi, vnd also von dergleichen mehr. Atqui nolim eos, etsi Boccatium Auctorem habeant hoc imitari, Aber ich wolte nicht densel-bigen, ob sie gleich Boccatium zu einem Vorgeher haben, disem nachthun, Cum eiusmodi dicendi genus, sit admodum affectatum. Weil diese Arth zu reden gar sehr animaßig, oder zu begier sichtig ist.
units.tr: Here it is to be noted that the Tuscans are accustomed to drop the letter I in words compounded with the preposition In, and to add an apostrophe to the vowel of the article, as Lomperatore, the emperor, in the singular, and in the plural, gli Imperatori, the emperors, and so of the others of this kind. But I would not wish to imitate them in this, although they have Boccaccio as their author, since this manner of speaking is very affected.

units.la: Deinde ex quo Apostrophus signum est vocalis amissae. Darnach weil der Apostrophus ein Zeichen ist, deß weggeworffnen vocalis, Ad quid Articulo, cui nihil deest adscribaretur. Zu was end solt er zum Articul, deme nichts mangelt, geschriben werden.
units.tr: Then, since the apostrophe is a sign of the vowel that has been lost, why should it be written on the article, which lacks nothing?

units.la: Adde cuiusmodi elisiones signum ad consonantes literas vocali quapiam privatas potius pertinere, quam ad vocales.
units.tr: Add that such a sign of elision belongs rather to the consonants that have been deprived of some vowel than to the vowels.

units.la: Zumal, weil ein solches Zeichen, der auß- gelassenen Buchstaben, zu denen Consonantibus, die eines Vocals beraubt seynd, mehr gehö- ren, als zum Vocali.
units.tr: Especially since such a sign of omitted letters belongs more to the consonants which are deprived of a vowel than to the vowel.

units.la: Denique dictiones illae Imperatore, & Imperatori, auferendi eis literam I. a qua incipiunt. Vnd wer- den demnach dise Wörter, Imperatore, &c. wann man den Buchstaben I. von welchen sie anfangen, hinweg wirfft.
units.tr: Finally, those words Imperatore and Imperatori are made by removing the letter I with which they begin. And so these words, Imperatore, etc., are deprived, if one drops the letter I with which they begin.

units.la: Indigne plebi capite (ut ita dicam,) videren- tur. Vnbillicher weise, jhres Kopffs also zure- den, beraubt. At adinstitutum, lo, rursus datur vocibus, qua incipiunt a duabus consonantibus diuersis. Aber wir müssen wider zu vnserm vor- haben schreitten. Das Lo wird wider gesetzt zu denen Wörtern, welche von zweyen vndersschidlichen Consonanten anfangen.
units.tr: They would be seen to be unworthily stripped of their head, so to speak. But we must return to our purpose: Lo is again placed before words beginning with two different consonants.

units.la: Quarum prima erit S. hoc modo, vnder wel- chen der erste ist ein S. als nemblich, solcher gestalt. Lo Spirito, der Geist, lo Stomaco, der Ma- gen, lo Scacciato, der Verjagte, l. ejectus, lo Stato, der Stand, lo Strale, der Pfeyl, Sagitta.
units.tr: The first of these will be S, in this form: Lo Spirito, the spirit; lo Stomaco, the stomach; lo Scacciato, the expelled; lo Stato, the state; lo Strale, the arrow.

units.la: Item prorsus intelligatur, de Articulo hoc, cum prapositionibus conjuncto. Eben difes ist zuuerste- hen, von disem Articul, wann er zu den Præpo- sitionibus gesetzt wird, als, Vt dello Spirito, deß Geistes, Spiritus. Allo Spirito, Spiritui, dallo Spi-rito, a Spiritu, dem Geiste, von dem Geiste, idem per lo Spirito, per Spiritum, durch den Geist, con lo Spirito, mit dem Geist, cum Spiritu, nello Spirito, in dem Geiste, in Spiritu.
units.tr: Likewise, the same must be understood entirely of this article when it is joined with prepositions, as Vt dello Spirito, of the Spirit (des Geistes), Spiritus. Allo Spirito, Spiritui, dallo Spirito, a Spiritu, to the Spirit, to the Spirit, from the Spirit, from the Spirit; idem per lo Spirito, per Spiritum, through the Spirit, con lo Spirito, with the Spirit, cum Spiritu, nello Spirito, in the Spirit, in Spiritu.

units.la: Datur tandem hic Articulus nomini Il quale, idque in principio Carminis, quare dicimus, lo quale; Endtlich wird dieser Articul dem nomini gegeben, Il quale, vnd daß zu anfang eines Verses, warumb wir denn sagen, nemblich vor Il quale, Lo quale.
units.tr: Finally, this article is given to the noun Il quale, and that at the beginning of a verse, which is why we say lo quale; Finally, this article is given to the noun, namely before Il quale, Lo quale at the beginning of a verse.

units.la: Articulus vero Il, præponitur vocibus, qua incipiunt a Consonantibus, ut, Aber der Articul Il, wird denen Wörtern vorgesetzt, so von einem Consonanten anfangen, als il Re, der Könıg, il Principe, der Fürst, il Cielo, der Himmel, &c.
units.tr: The article Il, however, is placed before words that begin with a consonant, as, But the article Il is placed before words that begin with a consonant, as il Re, the king, il Principe, the prince, il Cielo, the heaven, etc.

units.la: Vtrique postea datur quoque verbis infinitivi modi, Beyde werden hernach den verbis, so in infinitivi modi seynd, gegeben, seruata eadem ratione principium literarum, ut dicamus. Da die gewisse art der Buchstaben, einmahl wie das ander behalten wirdt, daß wir sagen, L'amare, das lieben, il dire, das sagen, lo scriuere, das schreiben.
units.tr: Both are afterwards also given to verbs in the infinitive mood, the same rule of the initial letters being observed, so that we say: L'amare, to love; il dire, to say; lo scrivere, to write.

units.la: Quod autem attinet ad Articulos istius quidem generis, sed numeri pluralis. Was aber die Articul belangt, so gleiches genuß haben, aber pluralis numeri seynd.
units.tr: As for the articles of this kind, but of the plural number, they have the same usage.

units.la: I. præponitur vocibus, incipientibus a consonanti, ut. Wird das I, denen Wörtern vorgesetzt,
units.tr: The I is placed before words beginning with a consonant, as

units.la: welche von einem Confonanten anfangen, als i Principi, die Fürsten, i Re, die Könige, i Cieli, die Himmel, &c.
units.tr: i Principi, the princes; i Re, the kings; i Cieli, the heavens, etc.

units.la: LI, vero & Gli, vel gli dantur vocibus incipientibus a vocali, vt. Aber das Li vnd Gli, werden gegeben denen Wörtern, so von einem Vocalen anfangen, als gli amori, die Lieben, gli honori, die Ehren, gli Efferciti, die Kriegesheeren.
units.tr: But Li and Gli, or gli, are given to words beginning with a vowel, as gli amori, the loves; gli honori, the honours; gli Efferciti, the armies.

units.la: Verumtamen cum litera vocalis, ex qua incipit sequens diffio fuerit I. Wenn aber der erste Buchstab, davon das folgende Wort anfangt, ein I. ist, Et præponendus est, Articulus Gli, so muß der Articul Gli vorgesetzt werden, qui tamen amittit suam vocalem, hoc modo, welcher doch seinen Vocalen verliert, auff dise weise, als Gl'iniqui, die Boßhaffrigen, Gl' impij, die Gottlosen, Gl' iniusti, die Vngerechten.
units.tr: But when the first letter with which the following word begins is an I, and the article Gli must be placed before it, it loses its vowel in this way, as Gl'iniqui, the wicked; Gl' impij, the ungodly; Gl' iniusti, the unjust.

units.la: Li & Gli præponuntur item vocibus, quæ incipiunt a duabus Consonantibus diuersis, quarum prima erit S. vt. Mehr wird das Li vnd Gli denen Wörtern vorgesetzt, so von zwenen vnderschidlichen Consonanten anfangen, vnder denen der erste ein S. ist, als Gli Spiriti, die Geister, Gli Strali, die Pfeyle, gli stenti, aerumnæ, die Mühseligkeiten, gli scommodi, incommoditates, die Vngelegenheiten.
units.tr: Li and Gli are likewise placed before words that begin with two different consonants, of which the first will be S, as. Further, Li and Gli are placed before words that begin with two different consonants, of which the first is an S, as Gli Spiriti, the spirits, Gli Strali, the arrows, gli stenti, aerumnæ, the hardships, gli scommodi, incommoditates, the inconveniences.

units.la: Idem omnino fieri necesse est, de his Articulis. Eben dises muß nothwendig auch geschehen, in disen Articuln.
units.tr: It is absolutely necessary that the same be done with these articles. This must necessarily also be done with these articles.

units.la: Cum
units.tr: With

units.la: Cum conjunctifunt praepositionibus, ut dicamus, wann sie zu einer praepositione gesetzt werden, als wenn wir sagen, de i Re, der Königen, & non degli Re, ac modo confimili per alios casus, und auff dergleichen schlag in andern casibus mehr.
units.tr: When they are joined with prepositions, as when we say de i Re, of the kings, and non degli Re, and in the same way in the other cases.

units.la: Sed hic observare licet, Aber allhier ist zubeobachten, solere plerumque ab articulo auferri I, & apponi Apostrophum, hoc modo, Daß das I. gemeinglich vom Articul werde wegk genommen, vnd ein Apostrophus darfür gesetzt, auff dise weise, De fatti tuoi, pro de i fatt tuoi, deiner Thaten.
units.tr: But here it is worth noting that the I is usually removed from the article and an apostrophe put in its place, in this way: De fatti tuoi, for de i fatt tuoi, of your deeds.

units.la: Ita quoq; vsurpatur, Eben daselbe wird auch gebraucht, in disen Arten zureden, als a', pro ai, da' pro dai, co' pro co i, ne' pro ne i, pe' prope i, denen, von denen, mit denen, in denen, vnd durch die, &c.
units.tr: The same is also used in these forms of speech: a', for ai; da' for dai; co' for co i; ne' for ne i; pe' for pe i: to the, from the, with the, in the, and through the, etc.

units.la: Verum judicio idfieri opportet, Aber difes muß mit bescheidenem bedacht geschehen, quod quidem legendus potius probatis Autoribus, welches zwar vilmehr durch lesung bewehrter Authorn vnd Scribenten, quam arte aliqua quis poterit adipisci, als durch die Kunst erlernet wird.
units.tr: But this must be done with careful judgement, which is learned rather by reading approved authors than by any art that one could acquire.

units.la: Dicimus praeterea, über daß sagen wir, delli Spiriti, & non dei Spiriti, agli Spiriti, vel alli Spiriti, non autem ai Spiriti, deren Geister, denen Geistern; Caeterum Praepositio per, vel Per, semper requirit Articulos Lo, Li, vel Gli. Ferners erfordert die Praepositio per, allezeit die Articulo s Lo, Li, Gli. Nulla prorsus habita ratione literarum, à quibus sequentes incipiant dictiones, vt, Da man gar nicht achtung gibt auff die Buchstaben, von welchen die nachfolgenden Wörter anfahen, Als per lo petto, per li fianchi, non autem, per il petto, per i fianchi, durch die Bruft, durch die Weichen. At non raro dicunt itidem, doch sagen sie auch nit selten, pei monti, pe' piani; loco earum dicendi formularum, qua habent, An statt difer Arth zureden, oder da sie so sagen solten, per li monti, per li piani, hoc est, per montes, per planiciem, Das ist, durch die Berge, durch die Ebene; Idem tandem Articuli Præpositionibus conjuncti, haud secus se habent. Vorgemelte Articul, wenn sie zu den Præpositionibus gesetzt werden, verhalten sich anders nicht. Ac cum ab illis disjuncti sunt, quare dicimus, Als wenn sie absonderlich wären, derohalben sagen wir, Dell' amore, degli amori, all' ingiusto, agli ingiusti, Der Liebe, deren Lieben, zum Vngerechten, zu denen Vngerechten, &c.
units.tr: We also say delli Spiriti, and not dei Spiriti, agli Spiriti, or alli Spiriti, but not ai Spiriti: of the spirits, to the spirits. Moreover, the preposition per, or Per, always requires the articles Lo, Li, or Gli, with no regard at all to the letters with which the following words begin, as per lo petto, per li fianchi, not per il petto, per i fianchi: through the breast, through the loins. But they not infrequently also say pei monti, pe' piani, in place of the forms of speech they have, or where they ought to say per li monti, per li piani, that is, per montes, per planiciem: through the mountains, through the plain. Finally, the same articles, when joined to prepositions, behave no differently. And when they are separated from them, we therefore say Dell' amore, degli amori, all' ingiusto, agli ingiusti: of love, of loves, to the unjust, to the unjust (men), etc.

units.la: Et eodem modo per omnes alios Casus, tam singularis, quam pluralis Numeri. Vnd also gleicher weise durch alle andere Casus, sie seyen gleich singul. oder Plurialis Numeri.
units.tr: And in the same way through all the other cases, whether of the singular or the plural number.

units.la: De Articulis autem Muliebris generis, illud sciendum. Aber von denen Articuln, die das Weibliche Geschlecht bedeuten, ist dises zumercken. Vt Articulus La, detur Nominibus, Communibus fere semper, vt cum dicimus: Daß
units.tr: But concerning the articles that denote the feminine gender, the following is to be noted. The article La is given to common nouns almost always, as when we say:

units.la: der Articul La, den gemeinen Wörtern fast im-merdar gegeben wird, als wenn wir sagen, La Tauola, La Barca, La Scuola. Die Tafel, die Bar-cke, die Schul. Et nonnunquam detur quoque no-minibus proprijs. Vnd zuweiln auch zu denen eigenen Namen gesetzt werde. Quemadmodum fecit Boccacius, dicendo, Wie der Boccatius ge-than, in dem er gesagt, La Belcolore, La Fiam-metta. Die schönfarbig, die klein flamm, &c. Vbi notare oportet, hunc Articulum poni integrum ante voces, quæ à Confonantibus incipiunt, Wobey zumercken, daß diser Articul werde völlig gesetzt, vor denen Wörtern, die von den Confonanten anfangen. Vt supra exemplis ad-duƈtis ostendimus, Wie wir in obeingeführten Exempeln erwisen.
units.tr: the article La is given to common nouns almost always, as when we say La Tauola, La Barca, La Scuola: the table, the boat, the school. And it is sometimes also given to proper names. As Boccaccio did when he said La Belcolore, La Fiammetta: the fair-coloured one, the little flame, etc. Here it must be noted that this article is written in full before words that begin with consonants, as we have shown in the examples brought forward above.

units.la: Sed tamen priuari Litera A. & donari Apostro-phe, quoties præponitur vocibus incipientibus à Vo-cali, hoc modo.
units.tr: But the letter A is nevertheless removed and an apostrophe given, whenever it is placed before words beginning with a vowel, in this way.

units.la: Iedoch wird das A. dem Articul La genom-men, vnd ein Apostraphum dárfür gegeben, so offt es Wörtern fürgesetzt wird, so sich mit ei-nem Vocaln anfangen, als da seyn, L' Anima, L' Onesta, L' amicitia, Die Seel, die Erbarkeit, die Freundschafft vnd dergleichen.
units.tr: However, the A is taken from the article La, and an apostrophe is put in its place whenever it is placed before words that begin with a vowel, as L' Anima, L' Onesta, L' amicitia: the soul, the honesty, the friendship, and the like.

units.la: Articulus verò Le, perinde se habet atque Arti-culus La, Aber der Articul Le, verhelt sich wie La; Nisi quod non datur nominibus particularibus, dicimus ergo, Nur daß er nit zu den eigenen Wör-tern gesetzt wird. Sagen derowegen, Le Stelle, Le donne, L' anime, L' amicitie, L' iniquita, L' imprese. Die Sterne, die Weiber, die Seelen, die Freundschafften, die Vngerechtigkeit, die fürnemmen Thaten.
units.tr: The article Le behaves just like La, except that it is not given to proper names. We therefore say Le Stelle, Le donne, L' anime, L' amicitie, L' iniquita, L' imprese: the stars, the women, the souls, the friendships, the injustice, the notable deeds.

units.la: Eadem penitus est, ratio, horum Articulorum, cum Prepositionibus conjunctorum, dicimus namque in sing. Num.
units.tr: The reason for these articles, when joined with prepositions, is entirely the same; for we say in the singular number:

units.la: Gleiche gestalt hat es mit disen Articuln, wenn sie zu denen Prepositionibus gesetzt werden, denn wir sagen in sing. Num, Della Stella, alla Stella, dalla Stella, per la Stella, con la Stella, nella Stella, Dell' anima, All' anima, &c. Des Sterns, dem Stern, von dem Stern, durch den Stern, mit dem Stern, in dem Stern, Item der Seelen, zu der Seelen, vnd dergleichen.
units.tr: It is the same with these articles when they are placed with prepositions, for we say, in the singular number, Della Stella, alla Stella, dalla Stella, per la Stella, con la Stella, nella Stella, Dell' anima, All' anima, etc.: of the star, to the star, from the star, through the star, with the star, in the star; likewise of the soul, to the soul, and the like.

units.la: In plurali autem Num. vnd in plurali sagen wir, delle Stelle, alle Stelle, dell' anime, all' anime, denen Sternen, zu denen Sternen, deren Seelen, zu denen Seelen, &c.
units.tr: But in the plural number we say delle Stelle, alle Stelle, dell' anime, all' anime: to the stars, to the stars, of the souls, to the souls, etc.

units.la: DE NOMINE.
units.tr: ON THE NOUN.

units.la: Von dem Namen, oder NennWort.
units.tr: Of the Name, or Noun.

units.la: Omnia Nomina Italica in aliquam exeunt vocalem. Alle Welsche Wörter gehen auß, auf einen Vocalem, als Dio, Angelo, Cielo, Huomo, & alia pene innumera; Gott, Engel, Himel, Mensch. Atqui eam aliquando amittunt, praesertim in vocibus, Aber sie verlieren denselben zu weilen, sonderlich in denen Wörtern, quarum postremam Vocalem praecedunt litera, quas Latini liquidas appellant, nempe &c.
units.tr: All Italian nouns end in a vowel, as Dio, Angelo, Cielo, Huomo, & alia pene innumera; God, angel, heaven, man, and almost countless others. Atqui eam aliquando amittunt, praesertim in vocibus, But they sometimes drop that vowel, especially in words quarum postremam Vocalem praecedunt litera, quas Latini liquidas appellant, nempe &c. whose final vowel is preceded by those letters which the Latins call liquids, namely &c.

units.la: Vor deren letzten Vocaln die jenigen Buchstaben stehen, so die Lateiner liquidas, zerschmelzende nennen, nemlich L. N. R. als debil, fel, mel, fedel, vàn, penfier &c. pro debile, fele, mele, fedele, vano, penfiero &c. schwach, Gall, Hönig, getrew, eytel, Gedanck; &c.
units.tr: Before whose final vowel stand those letters which the Latins call liquidas, the melting ones, namely L, N, R, as debil, fel, mel, fedel, vàn, penfier &c. pro debile, fele, mele, fedele, vano, penfiero &c. weak, gall, honey, faithful, vain, thought, etc.

units.la: Atque id fieri solet, vel cum vox sequens a Confonanti inceperit. Vnd difes pflegt zugeschehen, entweder wenn das nachfolgende Wort, von einem Confonante anfähet, als vàn desio, penfier vanuto, id est, vanum desiderium, prudens cogitatio, Das ist, vergebliche eytele Begürd, ein verstandiger weiser Gedanck.
units.tr: Atque id fieri solet, vel cum vox sequens a Confonanti inceperit. This is wont to happen when the following word begins with a consonant, as vàn desio, penfier vanuto, id est, vanum desiderium, prudens cogitatio, that is, vain idle desire, a prudent and wise thought.

units.la: Item fedel compagno, Mel dolce, ein trewer Gesell, süesses Hönig.
units.tr: Item fedel compagno, Mel dolce, Likewise, a faithful companion, sweet honey.

units.la: Sed non adscribitur Apostrophus, Aber kein Apostrophus wird dazu gesetzt, quod non amittant vocalem, propter alteram sequentem. Dieweil sie wegen deß nachfolgenden jhren Vocaln nit verlieren, qua propter dicimus:
units.tr: But no apostrophe is written for this, because they do not lose the vowel on account of the following one. Therefore we say:

units.la: Derowegen sagen wir, Gran Cosa, Buon Christiano, San Paolo, sine Apostrophi adjectione, ohne zuziehung deß Apostrophi, pro Buono Christiano,
units.tr: Therefore we say Gran Cosa, Buon Christiano, San Paolo, without the addition of an apostrophe, instead of Buono Christiano,

units.la: Buon Christiano, & Santo Paolo, San Paolo, qui dicendi modi sunt multo inelegantiores, welche Arten zureden, gar zu vnzierlich seynd.
units.tr: Buon Christiano, and Santo Paolo, San Paolo, which modes of speaking are far too inelegant.

units.la: Sed a Regula excipiuntur ista nomina. Von diser Regul aber werden außgenommen dise Wörter, Collo, Collum, Hals, Apollo, Volo, volatus, der Flug, Affanno, arumna, Trübsal, Inganno, dolus, Betrug, Obscuro, duro, & chiaro, dunckel, hart, klar, haud enim dicimus.
units.tr: But these words are excepted from this rule: Collo, Collum (neck); Apollo, Volo, volatus (flight); Affanno, arumna (trouble); Inganno, dolus (deceit); Obscuro, duro, & chiaro (dark, hard, clear), for we do not say them that way.

units.la: Denn wir sagen nicht Coll, Apol, Vol, Affan, Ingan, Ofcur, Dur, Chiar &c.
units.tr: For we do not say Coll, Apol, Vol, Affan, Ingan, Ofcur, Dur, Chiar, etc.

units.la: Quanquam his duobus posteremis per raro vsus est Petrarcha. Wiewol dise zwey letzen Petrarcha gar selten gebraucht.
units.tr: Although Petrarch has used the last two of these only rarely.

units.la: Neque truncati patiuntur ista voces. Auch können dise Wörter nicht zuftickelt werden, als Animo, Abisso, Pegno, Sosegno, Gemüt, Abgrund, Pfand, Stütze, & huiusmodi, vnd dergleichen vil mehr.
units.tr: Nor can these words be shortened, as Animo, Abisso, Pegno, Sosegno (mind, abyss, pledge, support), and others of this kind.

units.la: Solent deinde Italica nomina amittere postremam vocalem. Darnach pflegen die Italienischen Wörter auch den letzten Vocalem zuverlieren.
units.tr: Next, Italian nouns are wont to drop their final vowel.

units.la: Cum sequenti dictio a vocalium quapiam incepe-rit. Wenn das nachfolgende Wort von einem Vocalen anhebt.
units.tr: When the following word begins with a vowel.

units.la: Atque pro amissa vocali Apostrophus adscribi-tur, Sic: Vnd wird an statt deß außgelassnen Vocals, ein Apostrophus geschriben, nemlich, vostr'occhi,
units.tr: And in place of the dropped vowel an apostrophe is written, thus: vostr'occhi,

units.la: voßr' occhi, molt' anni &c. ewre Augen, vil Jahr. Ex quo apparet id in nominibus adjectiuis potissimum vsu venire, Worauß erscheinet oder erhellet, daß solches fürnemlich in den nominibus adjectiuis pflege zugeschehen.
units.tr: voßr' occhi, molt' anni, etc. (your eyes, many years). From this it appears that this happens chiefly with adjectival nouns.

units.la: Postremo, Poeta nonnulla privant nomina vltimis syllabis. Letzlich berauben die Poeten auch etliche Wörter in der letzen Sylben.
units.tr: Lastly, poets also deprive some words of their final syllables.

units.la: Nedum literis vocalibus aut ijsdem syllabis aufe-runt L, Geschweige deren Vocalium, oder nemmen auch von einer Sylben das L. gratia seruandi numeri inuersu, damit sie den Versß können erfüllen.
units.tr: Let alone the vowels, they also take away the L from some syllables, so that they can keep the number of the verse.

units.la: Hinc fit, vt dicam interdum. Daher geschichts, daß wir bißweilen sagen, Anima' & Animai, pro Animali, Laccino' & Laccuoli, Cana' & Canai, pro Canalli, Be' & Bei, pro Belli, Que' & quei, pro quelli, Ta' & Tai, pro tali, Qua' & Quai, pro quali, die Thiere, das Sail, die Sailer, Pferdt, Pferde, schön, schönen, jenige, jene, diesselbigen, dise, welche &c.
units.tr: Hence it happens that we sometimes say Anima' & Animai, pro Animali, Laccino' & Laccuoli, Cana' & Canai, pro Canalli, Be' & Bei, pro Belli, Que' & quei, pro quelli, Ta' & Tai, pro tali, Qua' & Quai, pro quali, (animal, animals; rope, ropes; horse, horses; beautiful, beautiful in the plural; that one, those; these; which, etc.).

units.la: Sed tamen id minime fit, Aber dises geschicht keines weeges.
units.tr: But this by no means happens.

units.la: Cum sequitur vox, qua a vocali incipiat, Wenn ein Wort von einem Vocal anfahende folget.
units.tr: When a word follows that begins with a vowel.

units.la: Vt passim probatorum Auctorum scripta fidem faciunt. Wie solches die Schrifften der gelehrten Männer, hin vnd wider bezeugen.
units.tr: As the writings of learned authors bear witness here and there.

units.la: DE NOMINUM FINIBVS. Von denen Endigungen der Namen oder Nennwörter.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE ENDINGS OF NOMES, or nouns.

units.la: Nomina substantiva propria virorum & Num. fingul. exeunt, in eigene Männer Namen Exempel, in singul. Num. wie sie sich im Italiänischen endigen, Als, In A. Enea, Pitagora, Luca, idem Andrea, Porsena. E. Cesare, Aristotele, Scipione, & Platone. I. Giovanni, Luigi, Dionigi. O. Alessandro, Pietro, Paolo. V. Gesu, Arta. E. Lione, Leon in Franckreich. I. Parigi, Brindisi, Ragusi, Paris, Brundis, Ragusa. O. Milano, Como, Pesaro, Meyland, Cemen, Pisauer. V. Corju, Cefalu, Peru, Corfun, Cephallen, Perus.
units.tr: Proper substantive nouns of men in the singular number end as the endings of men's names in Italian do in the singular. Examples: in A: Enea, Pitagora, Luca, also Andrea, Porsena. In E: Cesare, Aristotele, Scipione, and Platone. In I: Giovanni, Luigi, Dionigi. In O: Alessandro, Pietro, Paolo. In U: Gesu, Arta. In E: Lione, Leon in France. In I: Parigi, Brindisi, Ragusi, Paris, Brundis, Ragusa. In O: Milano, Como, Pesaro, Meyland, Cemen, Pisauer. In U: Corju, Cefalu, Peru, Corfun, Cephallen, Perus.

units.la: {f} A. Colonna, Carasa, Gonzaga, Cossa, Austria, Aragona. E. Dentice, Ponte, Este. I. Medici, Critti, Piccolomini, Venti, Tornaquinci, Doni. I. vel O. Quirini & Quirino, Soderini & Soderino, &c. I. vel E. Canalcanti, Canaleante, O. Auolo, Toledo.
units.tr: A: Colonna, Carasa, Gonzaga, Cossa, Austria, Aragona. E: Dentice, Ponte, Este. I: Medici, Critti, Piccolomini, Venti, Tornaquinci, Doni. I or O: Quirini and Quirino, Soderini and Soderino, etc. I or E: Canalcanti, Canaleante. O: Auolo, Toledo.

units.la: Caterum hæc Cognomina, non eodem modo vsurpantur. Aber dise Zunamen werden nicht auff einerley weise gebraucht. Quam ob rem quis eorum sit in dicendo vsus, haud abs re erit indicare. Darumb sihet es mich für gut an, anzuzeigen, wie man dieselbigen im reden soll gebrauchen. Dicimus itaque, Pompeo Colonna, Pompeius Columna. Derhalben sagen wir, Pompeius von der Säulen, Maria Colonna, Maria von der Säulen, Item il Colonna, der von Columna, oder von der Säulen, Columnensis, Colonnesi, Columnenses, die Columnefer.
units.tr: Moreover, these surnames are not all used in the same way. But these surnames are not used in the same manner. Therefore it will not be out of place to indicate how each of them is used in speech. So I think it right to show how these are to be used in speaking. We say, then, Pompeo Colonna, Pompeius Columna. Accordingly we say "Pompeius of the Column", Maria Colonna, Maria of the Column, likewise il Colonna, he of the Columna, or of the Column, Columnensis, Colonnesi, Columnenses, the Columnesi.

units.la: Dicimus proinde, Ferner sagen wir, Carlo d' Austria, quei della Casa d' Austria, Carl von Oesterreich, die vom Hause Oesterreich. Item Ferrante d' Aragona, quei d' Aragona. Ferdinand von Aragonia, die von Aragonia; Nam Aragonensi, significat etiam, qui eius Familia sunt studiosi. Dann die Aragonefer bedeuten alle die jenigen, so demselben Hause vnd Stamme wol beygethan vnd geslissen seyn.
units.tr: We say accordingly, Further we say, Carlo d' Austria, quei della Casa d' Austria, Charles of Austria, those of the House of Austria. Likewise Ferrante d' Aragona, quei d' Aragona. Ferdinand of Aragon, those of Aragon; for Aragonensi also signifies all who are devoted to that family and stock. For the Aragonesi signify all those who are well disposed and attached to that same house and lineage.

units.la: Quod ad alteram seriem spectat, dicimus. Was die andere Richtzen oder Reihe anbelangt, so sagen wir Camillo Dentice, Diana Dentice, il Dentice, & i Dentici, Camill Dentisch, Diana Dentischin, der Dentsch, die Dentschen.
units.tr: As for the other series, we say As for the other series or line, we say Camillo Dentice, Diana Dentice, il Dentice, and i Dentici, Camillo Dentice, Diana Dentice, the Dentice, and the Dentices.

units.la: Vnd widerumb, Andrea Ponte, vel da Ponte, Caterina Ponte, il Ponte, vel da Casa Ponte, quei da casa Ponte, Andreas von der Pruck, Catharina von der Prucken, die vom Haufe, von der Pruck.
units.tr: And again, Andrea Ponte, or da Ponte, Caterina Ponte, il Ponte, or da Casa Ponte, quei da casa Ponte, Andrea of the Bridge, Caterina of the Bridge, those of the house of the Bridge.

units.la: Item Ercole da Este, Caterina da Este, quei da Este, Deßgleichen Hercules von Este, Catharina von Este, die von Este.
units.tr: Likewise Ercole da Este, Caterina da Este, quei da Este, Hercules of Este, Catharine of Este, those of Este.

units.la: Tertij autem Ordinis, Cognomina ita vsurpantur, vt dicamus. Die Zunamen aber in der dritten Ordnung werden also gebraucht, daß wir sagen, Cosmo Medici, vel Cosmo de Medici, Lucretia Medici, vel de Medici, item il Medici, i Medici.
units.tr: But surnames of the third order are used so that we say But surnames of the third order are used thus: Cosmo Medici, or Cosmo de Medici, Lucretia Medici, or de Medici, likewise il Medici, i Medici.

units.la: Cosmus de Medici, Lucretia de Medici, die Medici, oder die Mediceer.
units.tr: Cosmus de Medici, Lucretia de Medici, the Medici, or the Medicean family.

units.la: Dicimus praterea, Vber diß sagen wir, Pietro Quirini vel Quirino, Camilla de' Quirini, non autem Camilla Quirini.
units.tr: We further say, Moreover we say, Pietro Quirini or Quirino, Camilla de' Quirini, not however Camilla Quirini.

units.la: Peter Quirinus, vel Quirino, Camilla de' Quirini, von den Quirinern. Non autem Camilla Quirini, quod non sit in vsu, nicht aber Quirini, weil nicht im brauch ist.
units.tr: Peter Quirinus, or Quirino, Camilla de' Quirini, of the Quirini. Not however Camilla Quirini, because that is not in use, but not Quirini, because it is not in use.

units.la: Rursus dicitur recte, widerumb redet mans recht, il Quirino, non autem il Quirini, verum si quis objecerit, cur recte dicitur il Medici, il Doni.
units.tr: Again it is rightly said Again one rightly says il Quirino, not however il Quirini, but if someone should object, why is il Medici, il Doni rightly said?

units.la: Wenn aber einer wolte einstreuen, vnd sagen, warumb sagt man denn recht, il Medici, il Doni.
units.tr: But if someone wished to raise an objection and say, why then is il Medici, il Doni rightly said?

units.la: Respondeo, quod Cognomina Medici & Doni, nullam aliam habent terminationem, quae sit in vsu, Deme gib ich zur antwort, daß die Zunamen Medici vnd Doni, keine andere endigung haben, die im gebrauch wäre.
units.tr: I answer that the surnames Medici and Doni have no other ending that is in use, To this I answer that the surnames Medici and Doni have no other ending that is in use.

units.la: Atqui cognomen Quirini habet & Quirino pro maribus, & Quirina profaminis.
units.tr: Yet the surname Quirini has both Quirino for men and Quirina for women.

units.la: Aber der Zunam Quirini, hat sowol Quirino von den Mannspersonen, als Quirina von den Weibsbildern.
units.tr: But the surname Quirini has Quirino for men and also Quirina for women.

units.la: Idcirco dicimus, derhalben sagen wir, Antonia Quirina, & non Quirini, cum tamen dicamus, Da wir doch sagen, Caterina Medici, & non Medica.
units.tr: Therefore we say Antonia Quirina, and not Quirini, though we do say Caterina Medici, and not Medica.

units.la: Exempla proinde cognominum quinta classis erunt, Mehr folgen Exempla der Zunamen nach der fünfften Ordnung.
units.tr: Examples of the surnames of the fifth class follow, Further examples of surnames of the fifth order follow.

units.la: Guido Canalcante, vel Canalcanti, il Canalcante, i Canalcanti, Veit Canalcant, der Canalcant, die Canalcanten, Iulius Canalcant.
units.tr: Guido Canalcante, or Canalcanti, il Canalcante, i Canalcanti, Guido Canalcante, the Canalcante, the Canalcanti, Iulius Canalcante.

units.la: Quod autem ad ea, quae in postremo loco posita sunt, dicimus. Belangende die jenigen, so zu allerletzt seynd gesetzt worden, so sagen wir Alfonsi & Amolo, Pietro di Toledo.
units.tr: As for those which are placed last, we say As for those which have been placed last, we say Alfonsi and Amolo, Pietro di Toledo.

units.la: Nomina appellativa, generis Masc. & Num. sing. die endigen sich in, &c.
units.tr: Appellative nouns of the masculine gender and singular number, which end in, etc.

units.la: A. Sofista, Poeta, Profeta, Podesta, Pianeta, Planet, Soffist, Poet, Prophet, Schultheiß.
units.tr: A: Sofista, Poeta, Profeta, Podesta, Pianeta; in German: Planet, Soffist, Poet, Prophet, Schultheiß.

units.la: E. Onore, Amore, Colore, Signore, Fante, quod est etiam gen. fem. & masc. Ehr, Lieb, Farb, Herr, Knecht, vnd Magd.
units.tr: E: Onore, Amore, Colore, Signore, Fante, which is also of the feminine and masculine gender; in German: Ehr, Lieb, Farb, Herr, Knecht, and Magd.

units.la: O. & E. Cavaliero, vt & Cavaliere, Poeta & multa alia nomina. Ritter, Poeten, vnd vil andere solche Namen.
units.tr: O and E: Cavaliero, and also Cavaliere, Poeta, and many other nouns. In German: Ritter, Poeten, and many other such nouns.

units.la: Est nomen pari, quod ad utrumque numerum & genus pertinet. Der Name pari, ist generis Communis, vnd utriusq; numeri, das ist singul. & pluralis, quare dicimus. Daher wir denn sagen, i pari tuoi, ipsi noştri, idem le pari tue, le pari noştre, hoc est tui, vel vestri similes, das ist deines vnd ewers gleichen, & hoc in num. plurali, vnd dises in plurali numero, nam in singulari dicimus, dann in singulari sagen wir, Tuo pari & Tua pari, id est, tui similes, das ist deines gleichen.
units.tr: The noun pari is of common gender and applies to both numbers, The noun pari is of common gender and belongs to both numbers, that is, singular and plural. Hence we say i pari tuoi, ipsi nostri, the same as le pari tue, le pari nostre, that is, your or your people's equals, and this in the plural number; for in the singular we say Tuo pari and Tua pari, that is, tui similes, your equal.

units.la: Dicimus praeterea, Vber dises sagen wir, vn paio di calze, due paia, tre paia, quattro paia di pol-li, ein baar Strümpffe, zwey baar, drey baar, vier baar junge Hüner.
units.tr: Moreover we say, un paio di calze, due paia, tre paia, quattro paia di polli, a pair of stockings, two pairs, three pairs, four pairs of young hens.

units.la: Ex quibus dicendi formulis perspicuum fit, Aus welchen Formen vnd Arten zureden erhellet, quod inter sit inter pari, paio, paia, was für ein vn-derschid vnder den pari vnd paio, paia, nempe pari similitudinem declarare, paio & paia, Societatem. tatem, vt ita dicam, nemblich pari, die gleichheit bescheine oder erklare, vnd paio, paia, die zwey-barung, oder bar Gesellschafft, also zureden.
units.tr: From these forms of speech it is clear From these forms and ways of speaking it is evident what difference there is between pari, paio, paia: what difference there is between pari and paio, paia. Pari expresses similarity, paio and paia a pairing or, so to speak, a companionship. That is, pari shows or declares equality, while paio and paia speak of a pair or a couple.

units.la: Sed de eo quoque admonebo lectorem, Difes aber muß ich den Leser auch erinnern. Has voces paio, pari & paia, pertinere etiam ad verbum, quod significat videor, hoc modo.
units.tr: But I shall also remind the reader of this. These words paio, pari and paia also belong to the verb which means I seem to be, in this way.

units.la: Daß difes Wörter pari vnd paia, gehören zu dem verbo, welches heist ich halt darfür, es bedünckt mich, der gestalt.
units.tr: That these words pari and paia belong also to the verb which means "I think, it seems to me", in this way.

units.la: INDICATIVI.
units.tr: INDICATIVE.

units.la: Io paio, ego videor, (videor mihi.) (videtur mihi.) Es hat mich bedeucht, ich hab darfür gehalten, ich halt darfür, mi pare, tu pari, e' ti pari, tu videris, Es bedunckt dich, (videtur tibi) es hat dich bedeucht.
units.tr: I seem, I think (videor mihi), it seems to me (videtur mihi): it has seemed to me, I have held the opinion, I hold the opinion. mi pare, tu pari, e' ti pari: it seems to me, it seems to you (tu videris), it seems to you (videtur tibi), it has seemed to you.

units.la: SVBIVNCTIVI.
units.tr: SUBJUNCTIVE.

units.la: Io paia, (che mi paia) wie mich bedeucht, daß mich bedeucht, ego videar, (vt ego videar) daß mich bedunckt, Tu paia, tu videaris, daß dich bedüncke, colui paia, ille videatur, daß jhm bedüncke, oder daß er sich bedeucht.
units.tr: Io paia, (che mi paia) as it seems to me, that it seems to me, ego videar, (ut ego videar) that it seems to me, Tu paia, tu videaris, that it may seem to you, colui paia, ille videatur, that it may seem to him, or that it seems to him.

units.la: Nomina Adjectiua, Numeri sing. & generis Viril. terminant in
units.tr: Adjective nouns, in the singular number and masculine gender, end in

units.la: O. Diuino, Bello, schön, Göttlich, Vmano Menschlich. Fiero, wild, Altiero, Hochfärtig, Orrendo graufamb, Ornato, Zier, Schmuck.
units.tr: O. Divine, Bello, fine, beautiful; Göttlich, divine; Vmano, Menschlich, human. Fiero, wild; Altiero, haughty; Orrendo, cruel, horrible; Ornato, adorned; Zier, ornament; Schmuck, decoration.

units.la: D
units.tr: D

units.la: In E, Celeste, Himmlisch, Fedele, Trewlich, ge-trewlich. Dolce, süß, virile, männlich, quae sunt item muliebris generis, welche dise in E. auch im Italienischen, gen. fem. seyndt.
units.tr: In E: Celeste, heavenly; Fedele, faithful, trusty; dolce, sweet; virile, manly. These are likewise of the feminine gender too, as is the case with the ones ending in E in Italian.

units.la: Quantum vero attinet ad eadem nomina, Was aber eben dise Wörter anbelanget. Cum numeri sint multitudinis, omnia in I. exeunt, ut.
units.tr: As for these same nouns, when they are in the plural number, all end in I.

units.la: Wenn sie plural. num. seynd, so gehen sie alle auff ein I, auß, als Huomini, Cieli, Angeli, &c. Menschen, Himmel, Engel, &c.
units.tr: When the nominatives plural end in I, they all go out in -i, as Huomini, Cieli, Angeli, etc.: men, heavens, angels, etc.

units.la: Atque id intelligatur, Vnd ist dises zuverste-hen, tam si in singulari numero finiant in O, quam si in aliis terminentur literis vocalibus, sowol wenn sie sich in singulari numero auff ein O, als auff ei-nen selbst lautenden Buchstaben enden.
units.tr: And this is to be understood as applying both when they end in the singular in O and when they end in another vowel letter.

units.la: Excipiuntur tamen ea, Iedoch werden außgenommen die jenigen, qua in numero multitudinis duplicem habent finem in I.
units.tr: Nevertheless, the following are excepted, which have a double ending in I in the plural.

units.la: So in plurali numero, zweyerley endigungen haben in I.
units.tr: That is, those which have two endings in I in the plural.

units.la: Scilicet ac generis sunt virilis, vnd in A. Nemblichen, vnd seynd Männlichen Geschlechts, vnd in A.
units.tr: Namely, those which are of the masculine gender and end in A.

units.la: Quomodo genus mutant ex virili in muliebre, Da sie das Geschlecht auß dem Männlichen in das Weibliche verändern, qua omnia subjecta typo ob oculos ponuntur.
units.tr: Since they change their gender from masculine to feminine, all of which are set before the eyes in the table below.

units.la: Welches alles auß hie vndergesetzter Taffel, augenscheinlich gemacht wird.
units.tr: All of this is made plain by the table set out below.

units.la: Sed quæ definiunt in A, magis & frequentius vsur-pant, Aber welche auff ein A, außgehen, (wie obstehend zusehen) werden mehr vnd öffter gebraucht, von denen, qui versantur in soluta Oratione, welche mit vngebundener Rede vmbgehen.
units.tr: But those which end in A are used more and more often, but those which end in A (as seen above) are used more and more often, by those who deal in unbound speech, that is, in prose.

units.la: Porro & nomina muliebris generis, haud eodem modo finiunt. Vber das gehen die Namen Weib-lichesGeschlechts, nicht auff einerley weise auß, vt subiectli Typi ostendunt, wie die allhie beygefügten Figuren außweisen.
units.tr: Moreover, nouns of the feminine gender do not all end in the same way, as the figures set alongside here show.

units.la: Nomina propria mulierum, Weiber Namen Exempla, singular, numeri definunt. A, Cornelia, Laura, Tullia, Lucretia, Maria, &c. E, Beatrice, Rachele, Berenice, Penelope, O, Glicerio, Califto, Dido, Safo, Calipso, Iuno.
units.tr: Proper names of women, examples in the singular number. A: Cornelia, Laura, Tullia, Lucretia, Maria, etc. E: Beatrice, Rachele, Berenice, Penelope. O: Glicerio, Califto, Dido, Safo, Calipso, Iuno.

units.la: Nomina Vrbium Mulieris generis, propria, Stätte Namen Exempla.
units.tr: Nouns of Cities of the Feminine Gender, Proper: Place-names. Examples.

units.tr: A. Roma, Vinetia, Padoua, Verona, Fiorenza. They end in E: Auignone, Cartagine, Atene. In I: Napoli, Constantinopoli. In O: Corinto, Sefto, Abido, Effefo, Argo, &c.

units.la: In A. Anima, Seel, Amicitia, Freundschafft, Donna, Fraw, Signora, Herrin, Herrliche Fraw.
units.tr: In A: Anima, soul; Amicitia, friendship; Donna, lady; Signora, mistress, a noble lady.

units.la: In E. Opinione, vt & Openione, Meinung, Lertione, Lesung, Affettione, Liebsneigung.
units.tr: In E: Opinione, also Openione, opinion; Lertione, reading; Affettione, affection, inclination.

units.la: In O. Mano, die Hand, La Mano.
units.tr: In O: Mano, the hand; La Mano.

units.la: In A. & E. Oneftà, Erbarkeit.
units.tr: In A and E: Oneftà, honesty, decency.

units.la: Arma, Waffen, Lode, Lob, Fronde, Blatt am Baum.
units.tr: Arma, weapons; Lode, praise; Fronde, leaf on a tree.

units.la: Frode, la Frode, Betrug.

units.la: Seruitute, Dienstbarkeit.
units.tr: Seruitute, servitude.

units.la: Grue, ein Kranck.
units.tr: Grue, a crane.

units.la: In V. Virtu, Tugend. Seruitu, Dienstbarkeit, Gru, &c.
units.tr: In V: Virtu, virtue. Seruitu, servitude; Gru, crane, etc.

units.la: In A. & O. definiunt. Orecchia, & Orecchio, Ohr. Foglia & Foglio, Blatt, Blat. Cerchia, & Cerchio, Kreiß. Chiostra, & Chiostro, Kloster. Celsa & Celso, sind.
units.tr: They end in A and O: Orecchia and Orecchio, ear; Foglia and Foglio, leaf, sheet; Cerchia and Cerchio, circle; Chiostra and Chiostro, cloister; Celsa and Celso, are.

units.la: At in O. cum definunt, Virilis sunt generis. Aber wann sie auff ein O. außgehn, seynd sie Männlichen Geschlechts; Atque Orecchia & Foglia, infrequenti sunt visu, sicut, &c. Vnd sind gar sehr gebräuchlich, wie auch Cerchio, Kreiß, Chiostro, Kloster, oder verspperrt Gemach. Catera vero non item, aber die andern nicht also.
units.tr: But when they end in O, they are of the masculine gender. But when they end in an O, they are masculine. Orecchia and Foglia are rarely seen, as, etc. Yet Cerchio, circle, and Chiostro, cloister, or a closed room, are very much in use. The others are not so.

units.la: Nomina generis Muliebris adjectiua, singularis Numeri. Namen Weiblichen Geschlechts, so Adjectiua genennt werden. Definunt in A. als da seyn.
units.tr: Adjectival nouns of the feminine gender, singular number. Feminine nouns, which are called adjectives. They end in A, as follows.

units.la: A. Bianca, Bella, Diuina, Ornata, Fiera, Rea & Ria. Die Weiße, die Schone, die Göttliche, die gezierte, die wilde, die Boßhafftige.
units.tr: A. Bianca, Bella, Diuina, Ornata, Fiera, Rea and Ria: the white, the beautiful, the divine, the adorned, the wild, the wicked.

units.la: E. La Fedele, Crudele, Forte, qua & Virilis generis sunt. Die getrewe, oder getreuliche, die greuliche, die starcke, so auch Männliches Geschlechts seynd.
units.tr: E. La Fedele, Crudele, Forte, which are also of the masculine gender: the faithful (or faithfully), the cruel, the strong.

units.la: Caterum in Multitudinis numero huiusmodi Nomina habebant I. postremo loco.
units.tr: Otherwise, in the plural number, such names had I in the last place.

units.la: Aber in plurali Num. haben solche vnd dergleichen Namen das I. zu end, si in singulari habebunt E. Wann sie in sing. das E. haben.
units.tr: But in the plural number such and similar names have I at the end, if in the singular they have E.

units.la: Quod in singulari habebunt A. in plurali habebunt E. Wann sie in sing. das A. haben, werden sie in plurali das E. haben.
units.tr: That in the singular they will have A, in the plural they will have E. When they have A in the singular, they will have E in the plural.

units.la: Hinc fit, vt qua habent in sing. duplicem finem, eundem habeant quoque duplicem in plurali Num. Dahero geschicht es, daß welche zweyerley endung haben in sing. num. daß solche auch in plurali zwo endungen haben.
units.tr: Hence it follows that those which have two endings in the singular number have likewise two endings in the plural. This is why it happens that those words which have two endings in the singular also have two endings in the plural.

La Orec-chio, & L'Orecchio, the same. | Plur. | & Le Orecchia, I. Le Orecchi, the same.

units.la: Verum, mano, ex quodam vsu loquendi quamuis sit generis Muliebris, definit tamen, cum singularis est numerus, in O. vt mano. Aber Mano, ob es gleich generis foeminini ist, gehet es doch auff eine beweise zureden, in singulari numero auff ein O auß, als Mano, la Mano, die Hand.
units.tr: But mano, by a certain usage of speech, although it is of the feminine gender, nevertheless ends in O in the singular number, as mano. But Mano, although it is of the feminine gender, in the singular number ends in an O, as Mano, la Mano, the hand.

units.la: Ex quo consequitur, in plurali definere in I, vt Mani.
units.tr: From which it follows that in the plural it ends in I, as Mani.

units.la: Darauß folget, es muß in plurali numero I. haben, als Le mani, die Hände, oder Hende.
units.tr: From this it follows that it must have I in the plural, as Le mani, the hands.

units.la: DE NOMINVM DE- CLINATIONE.
units.tr: On the Declension of Nouns.

units.la: Von der Declination oder ab- wandlung der Namen.
units.tr: On the declension, or inflection, of nouns.

units.la: QVanquam, (vt supra monuimus,) Ob zwar, wie oben erwehnet, cum de Articulorum declinatione ageremus. Davon der Declination der Geschlechtswörter, oder von den Articuln gehandelt worden.
units.tr: Although, as we noted above, although, as mentioned above, when we treated the declension of the articles. That is, the declension of the gender words, or articles, has been dealt with.

units.la: Sermo Italicus casus & flexus nominum, eiusmodi in Latina & Graeca Linguis esse videntur non agnoscat.
units.tr: The Italian language does not recognise case and inflection of nouns of the kind found in Latin and Greek.

units.la: Die Italienische Sprache, keine fälle, (casus) oder Windungen der Namen hat, wie die Lateinische vnd Griechische Sprachen haben.
units.tr: The Italian language has no cases (casus) or inflections of nouns, as Latin and Greek have.

units.la: Nihilominus haud omnem inflexionem respuit, So verwirffet sie jedoch die Wörterbeugungen nicht gantz vnd gar.
units.tr: Nevertheless it does not reject inflection altogether, nor does it wholly refuse changes in the form of words.

units.la: Nam eam habet, quae vel ex praepositionibus solis, vel ex ijsdem vna cum Articulis pendet. Denn sie hat je dise, so entweder allein an denen praepositionibus, oder aber auff disem vnd jenem Articul zugleich hanget.
units.tr: For it has that inflection which depends either on prepositions alone, or on the same together with the articles. For it has those forms which depend either on the praepositionibus alone, or on this or that article as well.

units.la: Cuius rei Paradigmata aliquot adscribam. Dessen wir etliche Exempelstaffeln wollen hieher setzen.
units.tr: I shall add some paradigms of this matter. We will set down here several tables of examples.

units.la: Paradigma oder Vorstellung I. ex Artic. cum praepositione.
units.tr: Paradigm or Illustration I. of the Article with a Preposition.

units.la: Nom. sing. L' amico, amicus, der Freundt.Gen. Dell' amico, amici, deß Freundts.Dat. All' amico, amico, dem Freunde.Accus. L' amico, amicum, den Freundt.Vocat. O, amico, amice, O Freundt.Ablat. Dall' amico, ab amico, von dem Freund.
units.tr: Nom. sing. The friend; Gen. of the friend; Dat. to the friend; Accus. the friend; Vocat. O friend; Ablat. from the friend.

units.la: Plur. Nom. Gli amici, amici, die Freunde.Gen. Degli amici, amicorum, deren Freunde.Dat. Agli amici, amicis, denen Freunden.Accus. Gli amici, amicos, die Freunde.Vocat. O amici, amici, O jhr Freunde.Ablat. Dagli amici, ab amicis, von denen Freunden.
units.tr: Plur. Nom. the friends; Gen. of the friends; Dat. to the friends; Accus. the friends; Vocat. O you friends; Ablat. from the friends.

units.la: I. Paradigmatis usus, per omnes casus & numeros.
units.tr: I. Use of the paradigm through all cases and numbers.

units.la: Fürbildungs Taffel gebrauch, durch alle casus vnd numeros.
units.tr: Use of the paradigm table through all cases and numbers.

units.la: Nom. sing. L' amico venne, amicus venit, der Freund ist kommen.
units.tr: Nominative singular: The friend came; the friend came, the friend has come.

units.la: Genit. Mi ricordo dell' amico, memini amici, Ich erinnere mich deß Freundts.
units.tr: Genitive: I remember the friend; I remember of the friend, I remember the friend.

units.la: Dat. Compiaccio all' amico, morem gero amico, ich gefall dem Freunde.
units.tr: Dative: I please the friend; I obey the friend, I please the friend.

units.la: Accus. Amo l' amico, amicum amo, ich liebe den Freund.
units.tr: Accusative: I love the friend; I love the friend, I love the friend.

units.la: Vocat. O amico vieni, o amice veni, O Freund komm.
units.tr: Vocative: O friend, come; O friend, come, O friend, come.

units.la: Ablat. Mi parto dell' amico, discedo ab amico, ich scheide vom Freunde.
units.tr: Ablative: I part from the friend; I depart from the friend, I part from the friend.

units.la: Nom. plur. gli amici vennero, amici venerunt, die Freunde seynd kommen.
units.tr: Nominative plural: The friends came; the friends came, the friends have come.

units.la: Genit. Mi ricordo degli amici, memini amicorum, ich erinnere mich der Freunde.
units.tr: Genitive: I remember the friends; I remember of the friends, I remember the friends.

units.la: Dativ. Compiaccio agli amici, amicis morem gero, ich gefall den Freunden.
units.tr: Dative: I please the friends; I obey the friends, I please the friends.

units.la: Accus. Amo gli amici, amicos amo, ich lieb die Freunde.
units.tr: Accusative: I love the friends; I love the friends, I love the friends.

units.la: Vocat. O amici venite, Lat. idem, O kombt jhr Freunde.
units.tr: Vocative: O friends, come; O friends, come (Latin: the same), O friends, come.

units.la: Ablat. mi parto da gli amici, ab amicis discedo, ich scheide von Freunden.
units.tr: Ablative: I part from the friends; I depart from friends, I part from the friends.

units.la: 2. Paradigma. ex prepositione sine Artic.
units.tr: 2. Paradigm, from the preposition, without article.

units.la: Vom Gebrauch der andern Tafel, ohne Artic.
units.tr: On the use of the other table, without the article

units.la: Nom. sing. Amico, der Freund, amicus.
units.tr: Nom. sing. Amico, the friend, amicus.

units.la: Genitiuo. di amico, ouer d' amico, amici, des Freundes.
units.tr: Genitive: di amico, or d' amico, amici, of the friend.

units.la: 2. Paradigmatis usus per omnes, &c.
units.tr: 2. Use of the paradigm throughout, etc.

units.la: Difer andern Vorstellungs Tafel gebrauch, allenthalben durchgehend.
units.tr: Another use of the example table, running through all cases.

units.la: Nom. sing. Fu amico vero, fuit verus amicus, ist ein wahrer Freund gewesen.
units.tr: Nom. sing.: he was a true friend, has been a true friend.

units.la: Genit. Ne e officio di amico, haud est amici officium, ist nicht eines Freundes Ambt.
units.tr: Genit.: it is not the duty of a friend, is not a friend's duty.

units.la: Dat. Io non parlai ad amico fidato, ich hab nicht zum vertrawten Freunde geredt.
units.tr: Dat.: I did not speak to a trusted friend, I have not spoken to a trusted friend.

units.la: Accus. mai non visitai amico a me più caro di te. Ich hab niemahls einen mir liebern Freund besucht, als dich. Amicum te mihi cariorem visitavi nunquam. Vocat. Amico vieni, komm mein Freund, Amice veni.
units.tr: Accus.: I never visited a friend dearer to me than you. I have never visited a friend dearer to me than you. I never visited a friend dearer to me than you. Vocat. Come, my friend; come, my friend.

units.la: Ablat. Da amico come sei tu, riceuo ogni cosa in buona parte. Von einem solchen Freunde wie du bist, nemb ich alles in gutem auff. Ab Amico tui simili, omnia in bona parte accipio.
units.tr: Ablat.: from a friend such as you are, I take everything in good part. From a friend such as you are, I take everything in good part. From a friend like you, I take everything in good part.

units.la: Superfedeo jam eodem modo exempla in numero multitud. afferre quod per se quisque ad instar adductorum in sing. Num. id praestare facilime poterit.
units.tr: I now pass over, in the same way, bringing forward examples in the plural number, since each person, following the examples given in the singular number, will very easily be able to do this himself.

units.la: Ich will jezund auff gleiche weise die Exempla plur. Num. beyzubringen vorbey gehen, weil ein jeder nach weise vnd arth, deren Exempeln sing. Num. ein solches leichtlich wird selbst thun können.
units.tr: In the same way I will now pass over bringing forward the examples in the plural number, since each person, by his own manner and method, will easily be able to do this himself from the examples in the singular number.

units.la: 3. Paradigma, ex Articulo Il.
units.tr: 3. Paradigm, from Article II.

units.la: Die dritte Fürbilde Tafel, aus dem Articul Il.
units.tr: The third paradigm table, from Article II.

units.la: Nom. sing. Il Maestro, Magister der Meister. Genit. del Maestro, Magistri, des Meisters. Dat. Al Maestro, Magistro, dem Meister. Accusil Maestro, Magistrum, den Meister. Vocat. O Maestro, O Magister, O du Meister. Ablat. dal Maestro, a Magistro, von dem Meister.
units.tr: Nom. sing. Il Maestro [Magister], the master. Gen. del Maestro [Magistri], of the master. Dat. Al Maestro [Magistro], to the master. Acc. Il Maestro [Magistrum], the master. Voc. O Maestro [O Magister], O master. Abl. dal Maestro [a Magistro], from the master.

units.la: Nom. plur. i Maestri, Magistri, die Meister. Genit. dei Maestri, Magistrorum, derer Meister. Dativ. ai Maestri, Magistris, denen Meistern. Accus. i Maestri, Magistros, den Meistern. Vocat. O Maestri, O Magistri, O jhr Meister. Ablat. Dai Maestri, à Magistris, von denen Meistern.
units.tr: Nom. plur. i Maestri [Magistri], the masters. Gen. dei Maestri [Magistrorum], of the masters. Dat. ai Maestri [Magistris], to the masters. Acc. i Maestri [Magistros], the masters. Voc. O Maestri [O Magistri], O masters. Abl. dai Maestri [a Magistris], from the masters.

units.la: 4. Paradigma oder Fürstellung, ex Nom. Muliebris gener. quod recipit Articulum La, priuatum sica Vocali Litera.
units.tr: 4. Paradigm or illustration, of the nominative of the feminine gender, which takes the article La, but deprived of its vowel letter.

units.la: Die vierdte Fürbilds Tafel, aus den Weiblichen Geschlechts Namen, durch den Articul La, mit benennung jedoch seines Vocaln Buchstabens.
units.tr: The fourth declension model table, from feminine nouns, with the article La, but with the naming of its vowel letter.

units.la: Nom. sing. L' anima, & Lat. die Seel. Genit. Dell' anima, anima, der Seel. Dativ. All' anima, anima, der Seelen. Accus. L' anima, animam, der Seelen. Vocat. O anima, & Lat. O du Seel. Ablat. Dell' anima, anima, von der Seel.
units.tr: Nominative singular: (Italian and Latin forms), the soul. Genitive: (Italian and Latin forms), of the soul. Dative: (Italian and Latin forms), to the soul. Accusative: (Italian and Latin forms), the soul. Vocative: (Italian and Latin forms), O thou soul. Ablative: (Italian and Latin forms), from the soul.

units.la: Nom. plur. L' animae, animae, die Seelen. Genit. Dell' animae, animarum, deren Seelen. Dativ, All' animae, animabus, denen Seelen. Accus. L' animae, animas, die Seelen. Vocat. O animae, & Lat. O jhr Seelen. Ablat, Dall' animae, animabus, von den Seelen.
units.tr: Nominative plural: (Italian and Latin forms), the souls. Genitive: (Italian and Latin forms), their souls. Dative: (Italian and Latin forms), to the souls. Accusative: (Italian and Latin forms), the souls. Vocative: (Italian and Latin forms), O ye souls. Ablative: (Italian and Latin forms), from the souls.

units.la: 5. Paradig. ex Nomine eiusdem quidem generis, sed quod recipit Articulum La, integrum. Die fünffte Fürbilde Taffel, aus eben demselben Geschlechts Namen, aber doch mit behaltung deß gantzen Articuls La, wie folget.
units.tr: 5. Paradigm from a noun of the same gender, but which takes the article La, in full. The fifth model table, from the same gender of noun, but keeping the whole article La, as follows.

units.la: Nom. sing. La Mente, Mens, das Gemüt. Genit. della Mente, Mentis, deß Gemüts. Dativ. alla Mente, Menti, dem Gemüt. Accus. La Mente, Mentem, das Gemüt. Vocat. O Mente, O Mens, O du Gemüt. Ablat. dalla Mente, Mente, von dem Gemüt. Nom. plur. Le Menti, Mentes, die Gemüter. Genit. delle Menti, Mentium, deren Gemüter. Dativ. alle Menti, Mentibus, den Gemütern. Accus. Le Menti, Mentes, die Gemüter. Vocat. O Menti, O Mentes, O jhr Gemüter. Ablativ. dalle Menti, Mentibus, von den Gemütern.
units.tr: Nom. sing. La Mente, Mens, the mind. Genit. della Mente, Mentis, of the mind. Dativ. alla Mente, Menti, to the mind. Accus. La Mente, Mentem, the mind. Vocat. O Mente, O Mens, O mind. Ablat. dalla Mente, Mente, from the mind. Nom. plur. Le Menti, Mentes, the minds. Genit. delle Menti, Mentium, of the minds. Dativ. alle Menti, Mentibus, to the minds. Accus. Le Menti, Mentes, the minds. Vocat. O Menti, O Mentes, O you minds. Ablativ. dalle Menti, Mentibus, from the minds.

units.la: Addam hic jam, Hier will ich hinzu setzen, quo passo ex omnibus Latinorum declinationibus, ad nos pleraque, quibus utimur, was gestalt auß allen declinationen, aller Lateinischen Wörter, die meisten, so wir gebrauchen.
units.tr: I will add here, in what manner, out of all the declensions of Latin words, most of those which we use are brought over to us.

units.la: Nomina derivantur, verum in hoc breuior ero; auff vns gebracht vnd geleytet werden, doch will ich kürtzer durchgehen.
units.tr: Nouns are derived, but in this I shall be briefer; they are brought over to us and led across, yet I will go through them more briefly.

units.la: Quam fortassis alicui res poscere videbitur. Als vielleicht die sach zuerfordern, einen gedunckem möchte.Tum quod breuitate studio, tum vero quod latinis literis instructus Lector, cum ex iis, quæ mox attigero, quasi ansam acceperit indagandi.
units.tr: Which perhaps the matter may seem to some to require, partly because I am eager for brevity, and partly because the reader, instructed in Latin letters, will from those things I shall touch on presently take, as it were, an occasion for inquiry.

units.la: Beydes weil ich mich der kürtze befleisse, theyls weil der Leser, so vorhin Lateinisch verstehet, so balden difem, was ich mit wenigen berühren werde, gleichsamb gelegenheit zu Handen fallen.
units.tr: Both because I apply myself to brevity, and partly because the reader who already understands Latin will, from the few things I touch on, have an opening presented to him.

units.la: Per se plura animadvertet, daß er dann selbsten vil ein mehrers darauß vermercken wird. Ex I. nom. vel vril. & mulieb. definentia in | A, Poeta, Propheta, Pitagora, Euangelista, Femina, Erba, Taula, Carta, Fenestra, E, Anchise, Penelope, Ex II. utriusq; gen. definentia in | O, Antonio, Virgilio, Milano, Canallo, Libro, I, Dionigi, Parigi, Luigi, Dionis, Paris, Ludwig. Ex III. definunt | A, Poema, Stratagema, Dogma, Gedicht, Kriegslist. I, Filli, Meri, irrig fluch, Gariddi, Tifi, eygene Namen. E, Cesare, Lettione, Pallade, Rachele, Niene, scure, Schnee, Beihel.
units.tr: He will notice many more things for himself, so that he will himself gather much more from this. From the first declension, nouns of either gender ending in A: Poeta, Propheta, Pitagora, Euangelista, Femina, Erba, Taula, Carta, Fenestra; ending in E: Anchise, Penelope. From the second, of either gender, ending in O: Antonio, Virgilio, Milano, Canallo, Libro; ending in I: Dionigi, Parigi, Luigi; Dionis, Paris, Ludwig. From the third they end in A: Poema, Stratagema, Dogma, Gedicht (poem), Kriegslist (stratagem); in I: Filli, Meri, irrig fluch, Gariddi, Tifi, proper names; in E: Cesare, Lettione, Pallade, Rachele, Niene, scure, Schnee (snow), Beihel.

units.la: E 2 Ex IV. O. Mano, Corno, effetto, affetto, eliffetto, rispetto, Hand.Horn, Werck, Begierd, Mangel, Ansehen. Ex IIII. quae definunt in Senso, Sinn, Giuefto, Recht, Intelletto, Verstand, Vdito, Gehör. In A. Vista, Veduta, das Gesicht, Vdita, die Hörung. Ex V. quae definunt in E. Specie, die gestalt, Effigie, Bildung, Temperie, Massigung, Congerie, Häuffung. l. Di Mezo di, des Mittags.
units.tr: E 2. From the fourth, ending in O: Mano, Corno, effetto, affetto, eliffetto, rispetto (hand, horn, work, desire, want, regard). From the fourth, those ending in Senso, Sinn, Giuefto, Recht, Intelletto, Verstand, Vdito, Gehör (sense, sense, right, right, understanding, understanding, hearing, hearing). Ending in A: Vista, Veduta, das Gesicht (sight, sight), Vdita, die Hörung (hearing). From the fifth, those ending in E: Specie (the form), Effigie (image), Bildung (formation), Temperie (moderation), Massigung (moderation), Congerie (heap), Häuffung (heaping). 1. Di Mezo di: of midday (des Mittags).

units.la: DE COMPARATIVIS ET SVPERLATIVIS. Von den Mitteln vnd höchsten StaffelNamen.
units.tr: On the Comparatives and Superlatives. Of the middle and highest degrees of comparison.

units.la: Sermo Italicus caret nominibus comperatiuus, sed eorum loco vsurpat positiuum cum Aduerbio piu, sic.
units.tr: The Italian language has no comparative forms, but in their place it uses the positive with the adverb piu, thus.

units.la: Die Welsche Sprach, hat keine Comperatiuos, oder StaffelNamen, sondern braucht anderen statt den Positiuum mit dem Adverbio piu, als also.
units.tr: The Italian language has no comparatives, or degrees of comparison, but uses the positive instead, with the adverb piu, as follows.

units.la: Piu dotto, piu bello, piu forte, gelehrter, schöner, stärcker, quorum insuper Significatio augetur additis Adverbijs.
units.tr: Piu dotto, piu bello, piu forte, more learned, more beautiful, stronger, whose meaning is further increased by added adverbs.

units.la: Derer Bedeutung noch ferner vermehret wird, durch die beygefügte Adverbia; als molto, & assai, vt assai piu, vel multo piu, vel assai molto piu, vil mehrer, vil fehrer, gar fehr mehr, gar vil mehr, vil höher vnd mehr, vnd höher gelehrter, molto assai piu dotto, omnibus hic enim modis recte dicetur. Vnd dergleichen weiß vnd arth aller rechtsamer gesagt wird.
units.tr: Their meaning is further increased by the added adverbs, such as molto and assai: vt assai piu, or vel multo piu, or vel assai molto piu; much more, far more, very much more, a great deal more, much higher and more, and much more learned, molto assai piu dotto. For in all these ways it will be correctly said. And in the same manner and fashion all such things are said in the correct way.

units.la: Quantum vero ad eorum vsum attinet, Was aber derselben brauch belanget, requirit Casum Genitivum, hoc modo, nemmen sie einen Genitivum zu sich, auffdiese weise.
units.tr: As for their use, however, they require the genitive case, and take a genitive after them, in this way.

units.la: Io son piu dotto di te, fum doctior te, Ich bin gelehrter denn du. Item, Cicerone fu piu eloquente di Ortensio, Cicero fuit eloquentior Hortensio. Der Cicero war beredtsamer, denn der Hortensius. Habemus etiam istos dicendi modos ex Comparativis, nempe vt dicamus. Wir haben auch diese Arthen zureden von den Comperatiuis, nemblich daß wir sagen. Tu non sei il piu dotto del Mondo. Du bist noch nicht der gelehrteste in der Welt.
units.tr: Io son piu dotto di te, fum doctior te: I am more learned than you. Item, Cicerone fu piu eloquente di Ortensio, Cicero fuit eloquentior Hortensio. Cicero was more eloquent than Hortensius. We also have these ways of speaking from the comparatives, namely when we say Tu non sei il piu dotto del Mondo. You are not yet the most learned in the world.

units.la: Item, Tu sei il piu ricco della Compagnia, Du bist der reichste in der Gesellschaft.
units.tr: Item, Tu sei il piu ricco della Compagnia: You are the richest in the company.

units.la: Item, io sono amico dei piu dotti, Ich bin ein Freund der Gelehrtesten.
units.tr: Item, io sono amico dei piu dotti: I am a friend of the most learned.

units.la: Item, Tu sei de i piu dotti, Du bist der gelehrteste einer. Tu ti puoi paragonare a i piu dotti, du kanst dich den aller gelehrtesten vergleichen.
units.tr: Item, Tu sei de i piu dotti: You are one of the most learned. Tu ti puoi paragonare a i piu dotti: you can compare yourself with the most learned.

units.la: Superlatiuum autem haud ita vsurpant, hoc est. Den Superlatiuum aber, brauchen sie keines weegs also, das ist, vt comparationem declaret, sed prastantiam, Daß er eine vergleichung bedeuten solte, sondern eine Vortreffligkeit. Non enim dicimus, denn wir sagen nicht. Cicerone su eloquentissimo de Romani. Cicero war der aller beredste bey den Römern. Cum huiusmodi dicendi genus sit plane latinus, Weil solche Arth zureden recht vnd pur Lateinisch ist, sondern wir sprechen, ma noi diciamo cosi. Cicerone su eloquentissimo. Cicero ist der aller beredeste gewest. Absq; adjectione alterius, ohne zusetzung eines andern, in cuius comparationem veniat, mit welchem der Cicero kōndte verglichen werden.
units.tr: The superlative, however, they by no means use in this way, that is, so that it expresses a comparison, but rather an excellence, for we do not say Cicerone su eloquentissimo de Romani: Cicero was the most eloquent among the Romans. Since this kind of expression is purely and plainly Latin, but we say ma noi diciamo cosi. Cicerone su eloquentissimo. Cicero was the most eloquent. Without the addition of another, with whom Cicero could be compared.

units.la: DE NOMINIBVS NVMERALIBVS.
units.tr: ON THE NUMERAL NOUNS.

units.la: Von denen Zahl Namen, vnd Zahlwörtern.
units.tr: Of the numeral names and number words.

units.la: VNo singulari, vni pluralis Numeri, & Viril. generis.
units.tr: One (uno): singular; (uni): plural; masculine gender.

units.la: Einer, ein, eine, die einen, in Mannlichem Geschlecht. Vnd vna, vne, im Weiblichen Geschlecht, als, die eine, die einen.
units.tr: One, a, one, the ones, in the masculine gender. And una, une, in the feminine gender, as the one, the ones.

units.la: At vsurpamus vno & vna, cum numeramus. Aber vno vnd vna, gebrauchen wir, wenn wir zehlen.
units.tr: But we use uno and una when we count.

units.la: Vni vero & vno hoc modo, vt dicamus. Vni aber vnd vno, auff dife weife, daß wir sprechen, Lune L'altre, vtraq, alle beyde Weiber, gli vni, egli altri, vtriq, alle beyde Männer.
units.tr: Uni and uno, however, in this way, so that we say: Lune, L'altre, utraque, both women; gli uni, egli altri, utrique, both men.

units.la: Hic animaduertas, haud secus hos dicendi modos ab Italoi vsurpari, atque Latini vsurpant, vtriq; & vtraq.
units.tr: You should notice that these modes of speaking are used by the Italians no differently than the Latins use utrique and utraque.

units.la: Allhier ist zumercken, daß dife Arthen zurechnen von den Italienern nichts, sondern von den Lateinern gebraucht werden nemblich vtriq, vtraq, sie brauchen obstehende gli vni, egli altri, oder Mulieb. generis, L' vne e L'altre, darfür.
units.tr: Here it should be noted that these forms of speech for counting are not used by the Italians at all, but by the Latins, namely utrique and utraque. In place of these, the Italians use gli uni and egli altri, or, in the feminine, L'une e L'altre.

units.la: Due & in Carmine si quis vult, duo, nunquam dua, vel duoi etsi nonnulli ea vsurpant.
units.tr: Due, and duo in verse, if anyone wishes; never dua, though some use duoi.

units.la: Due, in Versen, so jemand will, duo, niemals aber dua, oder duoi, ob gleich etliche solches brauchen.
units.tr: Due, in verse, if anyone wishes; duo, but never dua or duoi, although some people use them.

units.la: Caeterum pertinent ad vtrumq; genus, quod est intelligendum quoque de omnibus aliis numeris, qui sequentur.
units.tr: Otherwise they belong to both genders, which is to be understood also of all the other numbers that follow.

units.la: Ferner gehören sie zu beyderley Geschlecht, das ist, sie seynd generis Communis, welches auch von andern allen Zahlen, so nachfolgen werden, zuverstehen ist.
units.tr: Furthermore, they belong to both genders; that is, they are of the common gender. This is also to be understood of all the other numbers that follow.

units.la: Dicimus insuper ambidue, quod intelligitur de duobus maribus.
units.tr: We also say ambidue, which is understood of two males.

units.la: Vber daß sagen wir Ambidue, welches von zweyen Mannsbildern verstanden wird, vel altro faltem e duobus existente mare, oder doch von einem Mannsbilde vnder zweyen.
units.tr: Moreover we say Ambidue, which is understood of two males, or at least of a male out of two, that is, of one male among two.

units.la: Et Ambedue, quod de duabus mulieribus est intelligendum, vnd Ambedue, welches von zweyen Weibsbildern zuverstehen.
units.tr: And Ambedue, which is to be understood of two females; and Ambedue, which is to be understood of two females.

units.la: At Ambodue, Amendue, Amendune, & Amenduni, quamvis probati Auctores vtantur: Equidem haud libenter vsurparem.
units.tr: But Ambodue, Amendue, Amendune, and Amenduni, although approved authors use them: I would not be very willing to use them myself.

units.la: Aber ob gleich vornemme Leuthe, vnd Bucherschreiber, auch Amendue, Ambodue, Amendune sich gebrauchen, möchte ich es jhnen doch gewißlich nicht gerne nach thun.
units.tr: But although distinguished people and book writers also use Amendue, Ambodue, Amendune, I would certainly not like to imitate them.

units.la: Dicimus insuper Ambo, in eadem significatione qua Latini, Vber diß sagen wir Ambo, beyde, in gleicher bedeutung mit den Lateinern.
units.tr: Furthermore we say Ambo, meaning "both," in the same sense as the Latins.
